definition_zh: 成分；原料；（成功的）要素
definition_en: one of the substances that are combined to make a food, a product, or a successful result
core_image: 案板上一字排开的几样材料，正等着被倒进同一只锅里
scene: 厨房的台面上摊着食谱和一堆还没切的菜。The last ingredient was a spoonful of honey, stirred in at the very end.
sceneCN: 这里 ingredient 是「原料、成分」（第 1 个义项：混合制成食物或产品的材料之一）；句意为最后一样原料是一勺蜂蜜，在最后时刻拌了进去。图中可辨识物件：案板、刀、蜂蜜罐。

pos.zh: 名词：成分；原料；要素

derivatives.zh: 由本词加后缀构成，义为「就成分而言」
由本词加 list 构成的短语名词，义为「配料表」
由本词加动名词构成，义为「配料标注」

senses.title: Something put into a mixture
senses.definition: one of the substances that are combined to make a dish, a medicine, or a manufactured product
senses.definitionCN: 混合起来做成菜肴、药物或工业制品的物质之一
senses.example: Flour is the main ingredient in this bread.
senses.exampleCN: 面粉是这种面包的主要原料。
senses.why: Latin ingredi means to step into; an ingredient is what steps into the pot or the formula from outside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ingredi 意为「走进去」；ingredient 就是从外面走进锅里或配方里的那样东西。

senses.title: A part of a result
senses.definition: a quality or element that helps to produce a particular result or outcome
senses.definitionCN: 有助于产生某种结果的品质或要素
senses.example: Patience is a key ingredient of good teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是优秀教学的关键要素。
senses.why: The kitchen image travels: anything that steps into a result and helps form it counts as an ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 厨房的意象被搬了过来：凡是走进某个结果并参与构成它的东西，都算 ingredient。

intro.en: Ingredient is a Latin present participle that English borrowed whole; nothing was added or taken away.
intro.cn: ingredient 是英语整体借来的拉丁语现在分词，拼写几乎原样保留。

items.en: The root gradior meant "to walk, step", and it produced gradus "step" as well.
items.cn: 词根 gradior 意为「行走、迈步」，还生出 gradus「步、台阶」。

items.en: In- "into" plus gradi "to step" gave ingredi, "to step into, enter".
items.cn: in-「向内」与 gradi「迈步」合成了 ingredi，意为「走进、进入」。

items.en: The present participle ingrediens meant "entering", and was used of things that go into a mixture.
items.cn: 现在分词 ingrediens 意为「正进入的」，被用来指进入混合物中的东西。

items.en: English took the stem ingredient- directly from Latin in the fifteenth century, first in medical writing.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪直接从拉丁语取用词干 ingredient-，最初见于医学文献。

items.en: Cooking and industry later made it the everyday word for any stuff that goes into a product.
items.cn: 后来烹饪与工业让它成了指任何投入制品的材料的日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same stepping root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for what goes into a mixture.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「迈步」词根构成的词；近义组收其他表示「混合物中的东西」的词。

entries.definition: A slope or a gradual change of colour, built on the same root for step.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坡度、渐变」，词根同样是「步」。

entries.definition: Someone who has stepped through all the stages of a course.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「毕业生」，指走完了全部阶段的人。

entries.definition: A step on a scale, such as a rank or a mark.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「等级、分数」，指阶梯上的一级。

entries.definition: A part of a machine or system, usually technical in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部件、组件」，多用于机械或系统，语气偏技术。

entries.definition: A basic part of a whole, wider than ingredient and often abstract.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「要素、元素」，范围比 ingredient 宽，常指抽象成分。

entries.definition: The stuff something is made from, especially in manufacture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「材料」，多指制造某物所用的物质。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: ingredi is to step into: an ingredient steps into the pot.
normal.cn: ingredi 是「走进去」：ingredient 就是走进锅里的那样东西。

normal.en: The same root gives gradient and grade, all about steps.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 gradient、grade，都与「步、台阶」有关。

normal.en: Read the list of ingredients before you buy the packet.
normal.cn: 买包装食品前先看配料表。

normal.en: The main ingredient of a dish is rarely the cheapest one.
normal.cn: 一道菜的主要原料往往不是最便宜的那样。

normal.en: Patience is a key ingredient of good teaching.
normal.cn: 耐心是优秀教学的关键要素。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway into a pot: only the things allowed to step in end up inside.
abstract.cn: 想象锅上有一道门：只有获准踏入的东西才会进到里面。

abstract.en: An ingredient is never alone; it is defined by the company it keeps.
abstract.cn: 原料从不孤单，它的身份由与它同处的其他材料决定。

abstract.en: Results are cooked too: character, timing and luck are ingredients of success.
abstract.cn: 结果也是「炖」出来的：性格、时机与运气都是成功的配料。

examples.en: Mix all the dry ingredients in a large bowl.
examples.cn: 把全部干性原料放进大碗里混合。

examples.en: Trust is the most important ingredient in a partnership.
examples.cn: 信任是合作关系里最重要的要素。

examples.en: The label lists every ingredient in small print.
examples.cn: 标签用小字列出了每一种成分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因贵点」——因原料贵一点，做出来的菜才值钱

root: 拉丁语 ingredi「走进」由 in-「向内」+ gradi「迈步」构成，词根 gradior 又生出 gradus「步、台阶」（grade、gradual、gradient 同源）。现在分词 ingrediens 指「进入混合物中的东西」，英语十五世纪直接取用词干 ingredient-。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: what physically steps into a dish or product, and what figuratively steps into a result.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：实际走进菜肴或产品的东西，以及比喻意义上走进某个结果的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of materials waits at the edge of a pot, ready to step in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排材料在锅边等着踏进去。

branches.en: THE POT: whatever steps into the mixture counts as an ingredient.
branches.cn: 锅这条线：凡是走进混合物的都是 ingredient。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the same word lists what a medicine or a packet contains.
branches.cn: 标签这条线：同一个词也用来列明药物或包装食品里含有什么。

branches.en: THE RESULT: patience, timing and trust step into success as well.
branches.cn: 结果这条线：耐心、时机与信任同样走进成功。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT: an ingredient is always one part of a whole, never the whole.
branches.cn: 抽象这条线：ingredient 永远是整体的一部分，而不是整体。

branches.en: THE LINK: the concrete and the abstract senses share the idea of entering and combining.
branches.cn: 连接线：具体义与抽象义共享「进入并合成」的观念。

intro.en: Ingredient is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin stepping root, with a participle ending English kept intact.
intro.cn: ingredient 由拉丁语前缀与「迈步」词根构成，英语保留了分词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradior, gradi and ingredi are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European form is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gradior、gradi 与 ingredi 均有记录，只有更早的印欧形式属于重构。

items.example: It marks the movement towards the inside.
The verb supplies the image of a step.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「迈步」的意象。

items.example: The compound was the source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是本词的来源。

items.example: It gave English grade and gradual.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语 grade 与 gradual。

items.example: It keeps the word a participle in form.
items.exampleCN: 它让这个词在形式上保持分词。

items.example: Built on the same root with another ending.

items.meaning: to finish a course of study
items.example: The learner has stepped through every stage.
items.exampleCN: 学习者走完了每一个阶段。

items.example: The root survives again through Old French.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根又经古法语留存下来。

definition_zh: 内部的；里面的；内心的
definition_en: on the inside or closer to the centre; also used of private feelings
core_image: 一圈圈套着的同心圆，最里面那一圈几乎看不见
scene: 地图上用不同颜色标出了城区与外围。The inner ring of the city is closed to private cars.
sceneCN: 这里 inner 是「内部的、靠近中心的」（第 1 个义项：在里面的或更靠近中心的）；句意为城市内环禁止私家车通行。图中可辨识物件：地图、同心圆、路标。

pos.zh: 形容词：内部的；里面的；内心的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加最高级后缀构成，义为「最深处的」
由本词加副词后缀构成，文学用语，义为「在内心」
同族形容词，义为「向内的」

senses.title: On the inside
senses.definition: located on the inside of something, or nearer to its centre than other parts
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物内部或比别的部分更靠近中心
senses.example: The inner walls of the tunnel are painted white.
senses.exampleCN: 隧道的内壁被刷成白色。
senses.why: An old comparative of in, inner simply means "more inside" and later lost its compared force.
senses.whyCN: inner 是 in 的古老比较级，本义即「更在内的」，后来比较意味消失。

senses.title: Hidden and personal
senses.definition: belonging to a person's private feelings or thoughts rather than to the outside world
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个人私下的感受或想法，而非外部世界
senses.example: She drew strength from an inner calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她从内心的平静中汲取力量。
senses.why: The spatial sense turns inward: what lies inside the body is the self that others cannot see.
senses.whyCN: 空间的意象转向内部：身体里面的东西，就是别人看不见的自我。

senses.title: Of the part closer to the centre of a group
senses.definition: referring to the members of a group who are closest to its centre of power
senses.definitionCN: 指团体中最接近权力中心的成员
senses.example: Only the inner circle knew about the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 只有核心圈子知道这个决定。
senses.why: Groups are imagined as circles too, so their centre has an inner ring of people.
senses.whyCN: 团体也被想象成圆圈，其中心于是有了内圈人物。

intro.en: Inner is not a Latin word at all: it is an English comparative of in that has become an ordinary adjective.
intro.cn: inner 根本不是拉丁词，而是 in 的英语比较级，后来变成了普通形容词。

items.en: The Germanic preposition in- meant "in, inside" and is the base of inn, inner and into.
items.cn: 日耳曼语介词 in- 意为「在内」，是 inn、inner、into 的共同基础。

items.en: Old English had innera and inra, forms meaning "more within", used as adjectives and nouns.
items.cn: 古英语有 innera 与 inra，意为「更在内的」，可作形容词与名词。

items.en: Inner settled as an adjective in Middle English, no longer felt as a comparative.
items.cn: inner 在中古英语中固定为形容词，比较级意味已不再被感知。

items.en: The innermost form was added for the superlative, filling the gap inner had left.
items.cn: 为了表达最高级又造出 innermost，补上 inner 留下的空缺。

items.en: Modern usage adds the figurative senses of inner life, inner peace and inner circle.
items.cn: 现代用法又增添了 inner life、inner peace、inner circle 等比喻义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Germanic root for inside; the near-meaning group gathers other words for what is within.
note.cn: 形近组共享日耳曼语「在内」词根；近义组收其他表示「内部」的词。

entries.definition: Furthest inside, the superlative of inner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最深处的」，是 inner 的最高级。

entries.definition: Directed towards the inside.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「向内的」。

entries.definition: A place you go inside for the night.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「旅店」，同源。

entries.definition: Of the inside of an organisation, body or machine, more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「内部的」，多用于组织、身体或机器，较正式。

entries.definition: The inside part, especially of a building or a country.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「内部」，多指建筑或国土内地。

entries.definition: At the middle, the closest to a centre point.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「中心的」，强调位置居中。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the fact that inner is the old comparative of in, and the collocations it keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用 inner 是 in 的古老比较级这一点，以及它的常用搭配。

normal.en: Inner is just more in: the part further inside.
normal.cn: inner 就是「更在内」：更靠里面的那部分。

normal.en: Old comparatives lost their pairs: inner has no outer partner of the same shape.
normal.cn: 古老的比较级失去了配对：inner 没有形状相同的 outer 与之对应。

normal.en: The inner circle is the group closest to the centre.
normal.cn: inner circle 是最靠近中心的那个圈子。

normal.en: Inner peace is calm that no one else can see.
normal.cn: inner peace 是别人看不见的平静。

normal.en: The inner ear controls balance, not hearing alone.
normal.cn: 内耳不只管听觉，还管平衡。

abstract.en: Picture rings inside rings: the smallest ring is hardest to see from outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一环套一环：最小的那环从外面最难看见。

abstract.en: What is inner is protected by what is outer, and hidden by it too.
abstract.cn: 内在之物由外在之物保护，也因此被它遮蔽。

abstract.en: To know a person is to reach the inner room, which has no map.
abstract.cn: 了解一个人就是走进内室，而那里没有地图。

examples.en: The inner door had not been opened for years.
examples.cn: 那扇里面的门多年没有开过。

examples.en: Cycling gives her a sense of inner calm.
examples.cn: 骑车给她一种内心平静的感觉。

examples.en: The plan was decided by an inner group of advisers.
examples.cn: 这项计划由一个内部顾问小组决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一纳」——一切都纳在内部，便是里面的

root: inner 是古英语 inra / innera「更在内的」，即介词 in 的古老比较级，与 inn、into 同源；后来比较意味消失成为普通形容词，又造 innermost 表示最高级。比喻义有 inner life、inner peace、inner circle。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: physically inside, privately inside a person, and inside a circle of power.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：空间上的内侧、人内心深处的私密，以及权力圈子的内核。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rings inside rings, with the smallest one nearly invisible from outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一环套一环，最小的一环从外面几乎看不见。

branches.en: THE WALL: the inner wall faces the inside of a building or tunnel.
branches.cn: 墙壁这条线：inner wall 朝向建筑或隧道的内部。

branches.en: THE CITY: the inner city is the part around the centre.
branches.cn: 城市这条线：inner city 是围绕中心的那一片。

branches.en: THE SELF: inner feelings are the ones no camera can reach.
branches.cn: 自我这条线：inner feelings 是任何镜头都拍不到的感受。

branches.en: THE CIRCLE: power arranges people in rings, with the inner ring closest.
branches.cn: 圈子这条线：权力把人排成环，内环离得最近。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense measures distance from an outside towards a centre.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都在衡量从外部到中心的距离。

intro.en: Inner is a native English comparative; its endings are English, not Latin.
intro.cn: inner 是本族英语比较级，其词尾属英语而非拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Inner has no Latin source; the comparable Latin forms below belong to internal and interior.
latinIntro.cn: inner 没有拉丁语来源；下列拉丁形式属 internal 与 interior 的词源。

items.example: Another Latin way of saying inside.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语表达「在内」的另一种方式。

definition_zh: 无罪的；清白的；无辜的；（行为）无恶意的；天真无邪的
definition_en: not guilty of a crime or wrong; also free from harm or from evil intent
core_image: 法庭上被宣判无罪的人终于抬起头，肩膀一下子松开
scene: 旁听席上有人小声议论，法槌刚刚落下。The court found him innocent of all charges.
sceneCN: 这里 innocent 是「无罪的、清白的」（第 1 个义项：未被判有罪）；句意为法庭判定他所有罪名不成立。图中可辨识物件：法槌、旁听席、卷宗。

pos.zh: 形容词：无罪的；清白的；无辜的；天真的

collocations.zh: 未经证实有罪即视为无罪

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「无罪；天真」
由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「无辜地；天真地」
同根形容词，义为「无害的；无恶意的」

senses.title: Not guilty
senses.definition: not guilty of a crime or of doing something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 未犯某罪或未做过错事
senses.example: She was innocent of any wrongdoing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在任何过错上都是清白的。
senses.why: Latin in- "not" plus nocere "to harm" gives "not harming"; law applies it to a person who has done no wrong.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in-「不」加 nocere「伤害」，意为「不伤人」；法律用它指未做过错事的人。

senses.title: Harmless to others
senses.definition: not having an evil intention, or not causing harm
senses.definitionCN: 没有恶意，或不会造成伤害
senses.example: It was an innocent question, not an accusation.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个无恶意的提问，不是指责。
senses.why: If to be innocent is to do no harm, the adjective fits words and acts as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 如果 innocent 就是「不伤人」，那么它同样适用于言语与行为。

senses.title: Free of worldly knowledge
senses.definition: having little experience of the world and no awareness of evil
senses.definitionCN: 很少接触世事，对邪恶一无所知
senses.example: An innocent child played by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 一个天真的孩子正在窗边玩耍。
senses.why: The same word links a clean record with a clean mind that has not yet met temptation.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词把清白的记录与尚未遇到诱惑的纯洁心灵连在一起。

senses.title: An innocent person hurt by chance
senses.definition: someone who suffers from an event without being responsible for it
senses.definitionCN: 因事件受伤害而与事无责任关系的人
senses.example: The blast injured innocent bystanders.
senses.exampleCN: 爆炸伤及了无辜的旁观者。
senses.why: By-standers who did no wrong but suffered nonetheless are described by the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 没有过错却遭灾的旁观者，也用这同一个形容词来称呼。

intro.en: Innocent literally means "not harming", a Latin negative on the verb for doing harm.
intro.cn: innocent 字面意思是「不伤人」，是拉丁语动词「伤害」的否定形式。

items.en: Nocere meant "to hurt, injure", the source of noxious and obnoxious.
items.cn: nocere 意为「伤害」，是 noxious 与 obnoxious 的来源。

items.en: Innocens, in- "not" plus nocens "harming", meant "harmless, blameless".
items.cn: innocens 由 in-「不」加 nocens「伤害」构成，意为「无害的、无可指责的」。

items.en: Old French innocent passed the word into English with both the legal and the simple senses.
items.cn: 古法语 innocent 把这个词传入英语，法律义与朴素义并存。

items.en: English first used innocent of people who mean no harm; the legal sense followed in the courts.
items.cn: 英语最初用 innocent 指没有恶意的人，法律义随后在法庭确立。

items.en: Innocent now covers victims of accidents, harmless remarks, and childish simplicity.
items.cn: 现代英语中它能指事故受害者、无恶意的说法与稚气天真。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of harming; the near-meaning group gathers words for being blameless.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「伤害」动词；近义组收表示「无过」的词。

entries.definition: The state of being not guilty or not worldly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无罪、天真」。

entries.definition: Harmless, often in a slightly dull way.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无害的」，常略带「平淡」意味。

entries.definition: Harmful, especially to health.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的」，多指危害健康。

entries.definition: The opposite: responsible for a wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有罪的」，反义词。

entries.definition: Free of any fault, gentler than a legal verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无可指责的」，语气比法律判决温和。

entries.definition: Lacking worldly judgement, often a slight criticism.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「天真的」，常带轻微贬义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use nocere, the Latin verb of harming, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「伤害」动词 nocere，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: No harm done: in-nocent is "not harming", and that is the whole word.
normal.cn: 没有伤害：in-nocent 就是「不伤人」，全词的精义就在这里。

normal.en: Innocent of a charge, innocent of a lie: the preposition is always of.
normal.cn: innocent of a charge、innocent of a lie：介词固定用 of。

normal.en: The legal maxim is innocent until proven guilty.
normal.cn: 法律格言是 innocent until proven guilty。

normal.en: An innocent remark is the one you did not mean to hurt with.
normal.cn: innocent remark 是你无意伤人的那句话。

normal.en: Noxious is the same root without the negative: harmful.
normal.cn: noxious 是同一词根不带否定：有害的。

abstract.en: Picture a clean sheet of paper: nothing has been written, nothing has been done.
abstract.cn: 想象一张干净的纸：什么都没写，也就什么都没做。

abstract.en: Innocence is a verdict and a state of mind at once, one given by others, one by experience.
abstract.cn: 无罪既是判决也是心态，一个由他人给出，一个由阅历决定。

abstract.en: The word protects those who never intended the harm that reached them.
abstract.cn: 这个词保护的是那些从未想过伤害、却遭到伤害的人。

examples.en: The jury declared the man innocent of all charges.
examples.cn: 陪审团宣布该男子所有罪名均不成立。

examples.en: He lost an innocent bystander in the crowd.
examples.cn: 他在人群中误杀了一名无辜的旁观者。

examples.en: Her question was innocent enough, but it embarrassed him.
examples.cn: 她的问题本无恶意，却让他很尴尬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一诺森」——一句承诺森林般清白，便是无罪的

root: 拉丁语 nocere「伤害」加否定前缀 in- 构成 innocens「不伤害的、无可指责的」，经古法语 innocent 进入英语；同根词有 innocence、innocuous、noxious。法律义与日常义并存。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: not guilty, not harmful in intent, untouched by worldly knowledge, and harmed without cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：未被判有罪、无恶意、未知世事，以及无缘无故受害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean sheet of paper on which nothing bad has been written.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张干净的白纸，上面没有写过任何坏事。

branches.en: THE COURT: a verdict of innocent ends the case against a person.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：innocent 的判决终结对某人的指控。

branches.en: THE WORD: an innocent remark was not meant to wound.
branches.cn: 言语这条线：innocent remark 本不想伤人。

branches.en: THE CHILD: innocence as a lack of knowledge of evil.
branches.cn: 孩子这条线：innocence 也指对邪恶的无知。

branches.en: THE CROWD: innocent bystanders suffer what they did not cause.
branches.cn: 人群这条线：innocent bystanders 承受了并非他们造成的后果。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense turns on the absence of harm, whether intended, done, or deserved.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都绕开「伤害」——无论是有意、已做还是应得的。

intro.en: Innocent is a Latin negative prefix on the present participle of the verb to harm.
intro.cn: innocent 是拉丁语「伤害」动词现在分词的否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin nocere and innocens are recorded, as is the noun innocentia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nocere 与 innocens 均有记录，名词 innocentia 亦然。

items.example: It turns harming into not harming.

items.exampleCN: 这是英语 innocent 的来源。

definition_zh: 输入；投入（资源、意见）；输入端；输入数据
definition_en: something put into a system, such as data, effort, or money, or the act of putting it in
core_image: 一只手把数据卡片推进机器的进料口
scene: 技术员坐在电脑前核对屏幕上的一行行数字。The new software needs less input from the user.
sceneCN: 这里 input 是「输入」（第 1 个义项：输入系统的数据或指令）；句意为新软件需要的用户输入更少。图中可辨识物件：键盘、屏幕、数据卡。

pos.zh: 名词：输入；投入；输入端；输入数据
动词：输入（数据）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 device 构成，义为「输入设备」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「数据录入」
由前缀 out- 构成的对应词，义为「输出」

senses.title: Data put into a computer
senses.definition: information or instructions put into a computer or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 送入计算机或机器的信息或指令
senses.example: The program waits for input from the keyboard.
senses.exampleCN: 程序等待来自键盘的输入。
senses.why: Input is the noun of putting in: whatever is pushed into a system through its entrance.
senses.whyCN: input 是「put in」的名词：凡经入口推送进系统的东西。

senses.title: Effort or resources put in
senses.definition: the effort, money, advice, or time given to a project, often by several people
senses.definitionCN: 投入某项工程的努力、资金、建议或时间，常由多方提供
senses.example: The report was written with input from every department.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告是在各部门的意见基础上写成的。
senses.why: Factories speak of inputs of labour and materials, and meetings of inputs of advice.
senses.whyCN: 工厂说劳动与材料的投入，会议说建议的投入。

senses.title: The terminal that receives data
senses.definition: a place or device through which signals enter a system
senses.definitionCN: 信号进入系统的位置或装置
senses.example: Plug the cable into the audio input.
senses.exampleCN: 把线插进音频输入口。
senses.why: The entrance point takes the name of what passes through it.
senses.whyCN: 入口处往往就以流经它的东西命名。

intro.en: Input is not Latin at all: it is put with the prefix in- on the English model of output.
intro.cn: input 完全不是拉丁词：它是英语把 put 加前缀 in- 造出的词，与 output 对应。

items.en: Put has no certain origin even in Old English, where it appears in place names.
items.cn: put 连在古英语中也来源不明，只在地名里出现。

items.en: Input was formed in the eighteenth century for money and resources put into a business.
items.cn: input 在十八世纪造出，指投入企业的资金与资源。

items.en: Engineers took up the word for power and signals feeding a machine.
items.cn: 十九世纪工程师用它指供给机器的动力与信号。

items.en: Computing fixed the sense of data entered into a system, and output grew beside it.
items.cn: 计算机业固定了「输入数据」的义项，output 随之而来。

items.en: Everyday speech extended it to advice and effort contributed by people.
items.cn: 日常用语又把它扩展到人们贡献的意见与努力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words made with put and with the prefix in-; the near-meaning group gathers other words for contributions.
note.cn: 形近组收由 put 与 in- 构成的词；近义组收表示「贡献」的其他词。

entries.definition: What a system produces, the opposite of input.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「输出」，与 input 相对。

entries.definition: The act of entering data.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据录入」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: To bring goods into a country, with a Latin root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「进口」，形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Something given to a shared effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贡献」，指对共同努力的付出。

entries.definition: Information in a form a computer can process.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「数据」，指可供计算机处理的信息。

entries.definition: Money or effort put in for future gain.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「投资」，指为将来收益而投入的钱或力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain English build of the word, which is simply in plus put.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用这个词朴素的英语构成，即 in 加 put。

normal.en: Input is in plus put: what you put in.
normal.cn: input 就是 in 加 put：你投入进去的东西。

normal.en: Output sits on the other side of the same wall.
normal.cn: output 位于同一堵墙的另一侧。

normal.en: Ask for input before you write the report, not after.
normal.cn: 写报告之前征求意见，别等后面。

normal.en: Users type input; the computer answers with output.
normal.cn: 用户键入 input，计算机回以 output。

normal.en: An audio input is the socket that lets sound in.
normal.cn: audio input 是让声音进来的插孔。

abstract.en: Picture grain poured into a hopper: what goes in determines what comes out.
abstract.cn: 想象谷物倒进料斗：送进去的决定了出来的。

abstract.en: A system is only as good as the input it receives.
abstract.cn: 系统的质量取决于它接收的输入。

abstract.en: Every effort you put in is a kind of input, even when nobody records it.
abstract.cn: 你的每一点付出都是一种输入，即使没人记录。

examples.en: The form asks for input of your personal details.
examples.cn: 表格要求输入你的个人信息。

examples.en: We would welcome input from parents on the new timetable.
examples.cn: 新课程表方面我们欢迎家长提出意见。

examples.en: Insert the microphone into the input at the back.
examples.cn: 把麦克风插到后面的输入口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因普特」——因「普特」把数据输入了电脑

root: input 是英语用 in- + put 仿 output 构成的词，十八世纪指投入企业的资金与资源；十九世纪用于机器动力与信号，二十世纪计算机业固定为「数据输入」，后引申为「意见投入」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: data entering a machine, resources or advice entering a project, and the socket where signals enter.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：进入机器的数据、进入项目的资源与意见，以及信号进入的接口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grain is poured into a hopper; what goes in decides what comes out.
core.cn: 核心意象：谷物倒进料斗，进多少决定出多少。

branches.en: THE KEYBOARD: typing is the commonest form of input.
branches.cn: 键盘这条线：打字是最常见的 input。

branches.en: THE PROGRAM: a program cannot run without data from somewhere.
branches.cn: 程序这条线：没有数据来源，程序无法运行。

branches.en: THE MEETING: a good decision needs input from the people affected.
branches.cn: 会议这条线：好的决定需要受影响者的意见。

branches.en: THE FACTORY: labour, fuel and material are the inputs of production.
branches.cn: 工厂这条线：劳动、燃料与材料是生产的投入。

branches.en: THE SOCKET: the input is also the physical entrance.
branches.cn: 接口这条线：the input 也指物理上的入口。

intro.en: Input is a modern English compound; the prefix in- carries the sense of entering.
intro.cn: input 是现代英语复合词，前缀 in- 承载「进入」之意。

latinIntro.en: The form looks Latin but is English; the table records the native and Latin-related elements honestly.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词形似拉丁语，其实是英语词；下表如实区分本族要素与相关拉丁要素。

items.example: It marks the direction of the putting.
A verb of uncertain origin, recorded in Old English.
items.exampleCN: 古英语已有记录的动词，来源不确定。

items.example: It has no separate meaning now.
The partner word on the other side.
It forms inputted in some uses.
The same prefix in Latin words such as inject.
items.exampleCN: 在 inject 等拉丁词中也有同一前缀。

definition_zh: 询问；打听；调查；探究
definition_en: a question asked to get information, or an official investigation into something
core_image: 一个人探身向前，皱着眉向对面的人发问
scene: 服务台的电话一直响个不停，值班员一一记录。We received several inquiries about the new course.
sceneCN: 这里 inquiry 是「询问」（第 1 个义项：为获得信息而提问）；句意为我们收到了几份关于新课程的询问。图中可辨识物件：电话、登记本、台灯。

pos.zh: 名词：询问；调查；探究

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原，义为「询问；调查」
同根形容词，义为「好问的；好奇的」
同根名词，义为「审问者」
由动词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「询问者」

senses.title: A question
senses.definition: a question you ask in order to get information
senses.definitionCN: 为获得信息而提出的问题
senses.example: She made an inquiry about train times.
senses.exampleCN: 她询问了火车时刻。
senses.why: In- "into" plus quaerere "to seek" gives "a seeking into": a question is a search for information.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 quaerere「寻求」构成「向里寻求」：提问就是搜寻信息。

senses.title: An official investigation
senses.definition: an official process of asking questions to find out the facts about an event
senses.definitionCN: 为查明某一事件真相而进行的正式提问过程
senses.example: A public inquiry was held into the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 就那起事故举行了公开调查。
senses.why: When a whole institution asks the questions, the inquiry becomes an investigation with a verdict at the end.
senses.whyCN: 当一个机构来提问时，inquiry 就成了带结论的调查。

senses.title: Careful study of a question
senses.definition: the act of examining a subject carefully in order to understand it
senses.definitionCN: 为理解某一问题而进行的细致考察
senses.example: Scientific inquiry depends on evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 科学探究依赖证据。
senses.why: The same seeking applies to ideas: to inquire into nature is to look for its causes.
senses.whyCN: 这种「寻求」也适用于思想：探究自然是去找它的成因。

intro.en: Inquiry is a Latin compound meaning to seek into, and it covers both a polite question and a formal probe.
intro.cn: inquiry 是拉丁语意为「向里寻求」的复合词，兼指礼貌的提问与正式调查。

items.en: Quaerere meant "to seek, ask", the source of question, query and quest.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求、询问」，是 question、query、quest 的来源。

items.en: Inquirere, from in- plus quaerere, meant "to seek into, investigate".
items.cn: inquirere 由 in- 加 quaerere 构成，意为「向里寻求、调查」。

items.en: Inquisitio was a legal searching out of facts, the noun behind English inquiry.
items.cn: inquisitio 是法律上对事实的追查，是英语 inquiry 背后的名词。

items.en: Old French enquerre passed the verb to English as enquire and inquire.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 把动词传入英语，作 enquire 与 inquire。

items.en: The noun inquiry serves both everyday questions and official investigations.
items.cn: 名词 inquiry 兼用于日常询问与正式调查。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of seeking; the near-meaning group gathers other words for questions and probes.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「寻求」动词；近义组收其他表示提问与调查的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to ask or investigate.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「询问、调查」。

entries.definition: A single sentence that seeks an answer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「问题」，同根。

entries.definition: Eager to know and to ask, often about others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好问的、好奇的」。

entries.definition: A systematic official search for facts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调查」，强调系统、正式地查明事实。

entries.definition: A thorough enquiry, often by journalists or officials.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「探查」，常指记者或官员的深入追查。

entries.definition: The act of politely asking for something to be given.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「请求」，指礼貌地要求某物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use quaerere, the Latin verb of seeking, and the phrases inquiry appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「寻求」动词 quaerere，以及 inquiry 的常用搭配。

normal.en: Quaerere is to seek: an inquiry is a search, with words as the torch.
normal.cn: quaerere 是「寻求」：inquiry 是一次搜寻，言语就是火把。

normal.en: Question and inquiry share the root: one is a single question, the other a search.
normal.cn: question 与 inquiry 同根：前者是单个问题，后者是一次查寻。

normal.en: Make an inquiry is the polite phrase; hold an inquiry is the official one.
normal.cn: make an inquiry 是礼貌说法，hold an inquiry 是官方说法。

normal.en: British spelling often writes enquiry for a simple question.
normal.cn: 英式拼写常用 enquiry 指简单询问。

normal.en: A formal inquiry into the accident lasted a year.
normal.cn: 对这起事故的正式调查持续了一年。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held into a dark room: enquiry is light aimed at what is unknown.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯举进暗室：探究就是照向未知的光。

abstract.en: Every question is a small expedition into someone else's knowledge.
abstract.cn: 每个问题都是进入他人知识领域的一次小型远征。

abstract.en: Good inquiry asks without assuming, and listens without hurrying.
abstract.cn: 好的询问不预设答案，也不急着插话。

examples.en: We have had many inquiries about the job.
examples.cn: 我们收到了许多关于这份工作的询问。

examples.en: An independent inquiry was set up into the fire.
examples.cn: 就这场火灾成立了独立调查。

examples.en: Free inquiry is the basis of any science.
examples.cn: 自由探究是一切科学的基础。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因快瑞」——因想快点知道结果，就去询问调查

root: 拉丁语 quaerere「寻求、询问」加 in-「向内」构成 inquirere「探究」，名词 inquisitio 经古法语 enquere 传入英语，作 inquire 与 inquiry；同根词有 question、query、quest、inquisitive。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses on one thread: a question, an official investigation, and the careful study of a subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项串在一条线上：一个问题、一次正式调查，以及对某一课题的细致探究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp is held into a dark room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯被举进黑暗的房间。

branches.en: THE DESK: many inquiries arrive at an office that serves the public.
branches.cn: 服务台这条线：公共机构会收到大量 inquiry。

branches.en: THE LETTER: a written inquiry asks politely and waits for a reply.
branches.cn: 信件这条线：书面 inquiry 礼貌发问，静待回复。

branches.en: THE COURT: an official inquiry gathers evidence and publishes a report.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：正式 inquiry 收集证据并公布报告。

branches.en: THE LAB: scientific inquiry tests ideas against evidence.
branches.cn: 实验室这条线：科学探究用证据检验观念。

branches.en: THE THREAD: each sense is a structured search for what is not yet known.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都是对未知之物的有组织搜寻。

intro.en: Inquiry is a Latin prefix on a Latin verb of seeking, with a noun ending added.
intro.cn: inquiry 由拉丁语前缀加「寻求」动词构成，再加名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere, inquirere and inquisitio are recorded; the spelling with y is English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere、inquirere、inquisitio 均有记录；带 y 的拼写是英语的变化。

items.exampleCN: 这是本词背后的复合动词。

definition_zh: 昆虫
definition_en: a small animal with six legs and a body in three parts, such as an ant or a bee
core_image: 一片叶子背面，一只甲虫的身体被切成头、胸、腹三段
scene: 夏夜的灯下，小飞虫不断撞在玻璃上。A tiny insect crawled across the page and stopped on a word.
sceneCN: 这里 insect 是「昆虫」（第 1 个义项：身体三节、六足的小动物）；句意为一只小虫爬过纸页，停在一个词上。图中可辨识物件：叶片、甲虫、台灯。

pos.zh: 名词：昆虫

derivatives.zh: 由本词加表示「杀」的后缀构成，义为「杀虫剂」
由本词加表示「食」的词根构成，义为「食虫动物」
由 insectivore 加后缀构成，义为「食虫的」
由本词加 like 构成，义为「像昆虫的」

senses.title: A six-legged small animal
senses.definition: a small creature with six legs and a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen
senses.definitionCN: 有六条腿、身体分为头胸腹三部分的小生物
senses.example: Ants, bees and beetles are all insects.
senses.exampleCN: 蚂蚁、蜜蜂和甲虫都是昆虫。
senses.why: Insectum means cut into: Roman writers named the class by its visible segments.
senses.whyCN: insectum 意为「被切开的」：罗马作家按可见的分节为这一类命名。

senses.title: Any small crawling creature in loose speech
senses.definition: in everyday language, almost any small crawling or flying bug
senses.definitionCN: 在日常语言中，泛指任何小爬虫或飞虫
senses.example: Something insect-like moved in the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 有像虫子的东西在草丛里动。
senses.why: In loose use the word covers any creeping small creature, though spiders are not insects.
senses.whyCN: 在宽泛用法中它涵盖任何小爬虫，尽管蜘蛛并不属于昆虫。

intro.en: Insect is a Latin word meaning "cut into", given by ancient naturalists who saw the body in sections.
intro.cn: insect 是拉丁语「切开的」一词，古代博物学家见其身体分节而命名。

items.en: Secare meant "to cut", the source of section and segment.
items.cn: secare 意为「切」，是 section 与 segment 的来源。

items.en: Insectum, from in- "into" plus secare, meant "cut into" or "notched".
items.cn: insectum 由 in-「向内」加 secare 构成，意为「切开的、有刻痕的」。

items.en: Pliny and other Roman writers used insecta for animals whose bodies show cuts or segments.
items.cn: 普林尼等罗马作家用 insecta 指身体显出道道切痕或分节的动物。

items.en: English borrowed insect in the seventeenth century as natural history grew.
items.cn: 十七世纪博物学发展，英语借入 insect 一词。

items.en: Later science narrowed it to the six-legged class, while speech kept the looser sense.
items.cn: 后来科学把它收窄到六足纲，口语仍保留较宽的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of cutting; the near-meaning group gathers other small creatures.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「切」动词；近义组收其他小型生物。

entries.definition: A part cut from a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部分、切面」，同根。

entries.definition: A chemical that kills insects.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杀虫剂」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: To cut something apart in order to study it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「解剖」，同根。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a small insect, and a computer fault.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小虫」，日常用语，也指程序错误。

entries.definition: A kind of insect with hard wing cases.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「甲虫」，昆虫的一类。

entries.definition: An eight-legged creature, not an insect at all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蜘蛛」，八足，并非昆虫。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use secare, the Latin verb of cutting, and the collocations the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「切」动词 secare，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Secare is to cut: an insect is a body cut into three parts.
normal.cn: secare 是「切」：insect 就是被切成三部分的身体。

normal.en: Insect, section and dissect all come from the same cutting verb.
normal.cn: insect、section、dissect 都出自同一个「切」的动词。

normal.en: An insect has six legs, a spider has eight.
normal.cn: 昆虫有六条腿，蜘蛛有八条。

normal.en: Insect repellent keeps the mosquitoes away.
normal.cn: insect repellent 用来驱蚊。

normal.en: Insecticide kills insects, and insectivores eat them.
normal.cn: insecticide 杀虫，insectivore 吃虫。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf with a beetle on it, the body lined in three clear bands.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子上的甲虫，身体分三道清晰的纹。

abstract.en: The name is a description: nature was classified by its visible notches.
abstract.cn: 这个名字本身就是描述：自然按可见的刻痕被分类。

abstract.en: Small as insects are, they outnumber us and pollinate most of what we eat.
abstract.cn: 昆虫虽小，数量却远超我们，还为我们大部分食物授粉。

examples.en: Insects play a vital role in pollination.
examples.cn: 昆虫在授粉中起关键作用。

examples.en: He brushed the insect off his sleeve.
examples.cn: 他把袖子上的虫子拂掉了。

examples.en: This insect lives only in dry grassland.
examples.cn: 这种昆虫只生活在干燥的草原上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因塞克特」——因身上「塞」满了节段，才叫昆虫

root: 拉丁语 secare「切」加 in-「向内」构成 insectum「切开的、有刻痕的」，普林尼用它指体节分明的动物；十七世纪入英语，后科学上专指六足纲。同根词有 section、dissect、segment。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the strict zoological class, and the loose everyday word for a small bug.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：严格的动物学分类，以及口语里对小虫的泛称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beetle on a leaf, its body divided into three clear sections.
core.cn: 核心意象：叶上的甲虫，身体分为三节。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: insects are both pests and helpers in gardens.
branches.cn: 花园这条线：insect 在园中既是害虫也是帮手。

branches.en: THE CLASS: six legs and three body parts define the zoological insect.
branches.cn: 分类这条线：六足与三节身体定义了动物学上的昆虫。

branches.en: THE NIGHT LAMP: loose speech calls every small flying thing an insect.
branches.cn: 夜灯这条线：口语把一切小飞虫都叫 insect。

branches.en: THE PAGE: a crawling speck on a book is an insect in ordinary talk.
branches.cn: 书页这条线：书上的小爬虫在日常说法里也算昆虫。

branches.en: THE THREAD: in both senses the creature is small, many-legged and everywhere.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两种用法里，它都小而多足，无处不在。

intro.en: Insect is a Latin past participle used as a noun, with English compounds built on it later.
intro.cn: insect 是拉丁语过去分词作名词使用，后来在英语里构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin secare and insectum are recorded; the adjective insectus and noun insecta both appear in Roman writers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 secare 与 insectum 均有记录，形容词 insectus 与名词 insecta 都见于罗马作家笔下。

items.example: It marks cutting into the body.
items.exampleCN: 它标出切入身体的动作。

items.example: The root also gives section and segment.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根还给出 section 与 segment。

items.example: It appears in dissect and section.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 dissect 与 section 中。

items.example: The Latin source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是本词的拉丁语来源。

definition_zh: 插入；嵌入；（在文字中）添加
definition_en: to put something inside or between other things, or to add words to a text
core_image: 一枚硬币被手指推进投币口的窄缝里
scene: 打印机卡纸了，说明书上有一行加粗的提示。Insert the card face up and wait for the light to turn green.
sceneCN: 这里 insert 是「插入」（第 1 个义项：把东西放进或放进两物之间）；句意为正面朝上插入卡片，等指示灯变绿。图中可辨识物件：卡片、插槽、指示灯。

pos.zh: 动词：插入；嵌入；添加（文字）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「插入；插入物」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「可插入的」
由本词加前缀构成，义为「重新插入」

senses.title: To put inside
senses.definition: to put something carefully inside something else or between two things
senses.definitionCN: 小心地把某物放进另一物之内或两物之间
senses.example: Insert the plug into the socket.
senses.exampleCN: 把插头插入插座。
senses.why: In- "into" plus serere "to join, weave" gives "to join in": something is threaded into a place already filled.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 serere「连接、编织」，意为「编进去」：把东西穿进已经占满的位置。

senses.title: To add words to a text
senses.definition: to add a word, sentence, or paragraph to a piece of writing
senses.definitionCN: 在文章中增添词语、句子或段落
senses.example: Insert a comma after the first clause.
senses.exampleCN: 在第一个从句后加一个逗号。
senses.why: Text has its own gaps, so an insertion is a piece of writing threaded into the existing line.
senses.whyCN: 文字有它自己的空隙，所以插入就是一段文字被编进已有的行里。

senses.title: Something put in
senses.definition: a loose sheet, picture, or object placed inside something else
senses.definitionCN: 放在其他东西里面的散页、图片或物件
senses.example: The magazine came with a colour insert.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志附有一张彩色插页。
senses.why: The noun uses the same form and names the very thing that was threaded in.
senses.whyCN: 名词形式相同，指的就是被编进去的那件东西。

intro.en: Insert comes from a Latin verb of joining or weaving in, which is why it suggests careful threading rather than pushing.
intro.cn: insert 来自拉丁语表示「编入、接入」的动词，因此它暗示的是细心穿入而非硬塞。

items.en: Serere meant "to join, bind, weave", the root of series and sermon.
items.cn: serere 意为「连接、编织」，是 series 与 sermon 的词根。

items.en: Inserere, from in- plus serere, meant "to graft or insert, to weave into".
items.cn: inserere 由 in- 加 serere 构成，意为「嫁接、插入、编入」。

items.en: The noun insertio was used for grafting plants and for joining words.
items.cn: 名词 insertio 用于植物嫁接，也用于词语接入。

items.en: English borrowed insert in the sixteenth century for both planting and writing.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪借入 insert，兼用于种植与文字。

items.en: Modern use centres on cards, plugs, and paragraphs added to texts.
items.cn: 现代用法集中在卡片、插头以及插入正文的段落。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of joining; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of putting something inside.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「连接」动词；近义组收把东西放进里面的动词。

entries.definition: The act of putting something in, or the thing put in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「插入、插入物」。

entries.definition: A number of things joined in order.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「系列」，即依次连接之物。

entries.definition: To state something firmly, with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「断言」，形近但前缀不同。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for placing something inside.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「放入」，最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To join something to a group or a text without the idea of a tight fit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「添加」，不含紧贴嵌入之意。

entries.definition: To fix something firmly into living tissue or a mind.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「植入」，多指植入活体组织或观念。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use serere, the verb of weaving, and the phrases insert appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「编织」动词 serere，以及 insert 的搭配。

normal.en: Serere is to weave: to insert is to thread something into a place.
normal.cn: serere 是「编织」：insert 就是把东西穿进某个位置。

normal.en: Insert takes a direct object: insert a card, insert a comma.
normal.cn: insert 直接带宾语：insert a card、insert a comma。

normal.en: Insert into is the form used with a container.
normal.cn: 与容器连用时用 insert into。

normal.en: Insertion is the noun; reinsert means to do it again.
normal.cn: 名词是 insertion；reinsert 表示重新插入。

normal.en: A colour insert falls out of the magazine.
normal.cn: 彩色插页从杂志里掉出来。

abstract.en: Picture threading a needle: the fit must be exact, not forced.
abstract.cn: 想象穿针引线：要严丝合缝，不能硬塞。

abstract.en: To insert is to interrupt a line without breaking it.
abstract.cn: 插入是在不打乱整体的前提下在中间加入。

abstract.en: Writers insert clauses the way joiners fit new pieces of wood.
abstract.cn: 作者插入从句，正如木匠嵌入新的木料。

examples.en: Insert your ticket into the machine.
examples.cn: 把车票插入机器。

examples.en: She inserted a new line into the report.
examples.cn: 她在报告里加了一行。

examples.en: The book has an eight-page photographic insert.
examples.cn: 这本书有八页的摄影插页。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因瑟特」——因要把卡片「瑟」进缝里，便是插入

root: 拉丁语 serere「连接、编织」加 in-「向内」构成 inserere「编入、插入」，名词 insertio 用于嫁接与文字；英语十六世纪借入 insert。同根词有 insertion、series。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: putting an object in, adding words to a text, and the thing that is put in.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：放入物体、在文字中添加，以及被放进去的东西本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin is pushed into the narrow slot of a machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚硬币被推进机器的窄缝。

branches.en: THE SLOT: cards and plugs are inserted into narrow openings.
branches.cn: 插槽这条线：卡片与插头被插进狭窄的开口。

branches.en: THE GRAFT: gardening uses the same verb for joining a shoot to a stem.
branches.cn: 嫁接这条线：园艺用同一个动词表示把枝条接到树干上。

branches.en: THE PAGE: writers insert clauses and commas into a finished line.
branches.cn: 纸页这条线：作者把从句与逗号插入已有的行里。

branches.en: THE MAGAZINE: an insert is a loose sheet placed inside.
branches.cn: 杂志这条线：insert 指夹在里面的散页。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense describes something entering an existing order without replacing it.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都在描述某物进入既有秩序而不替代它。

intro.en: Insert is a Latin prefix on a weaving root, with an English verb ending preserved from Latin.
intro.cn: insert 是拉丁语前缀加「编织」词根，动词词尾沿用拉丁语形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin serere, inserere and insertio are recorded, along with series and sertum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 serere、inserere、insertio 均有记录，还有 series 与 sertum。

items.example: It marks the direction of joining.
It shows in insert and insert usages.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 insert 相关形式中。

items.example: The direct source of the verb.
A cousin from the same root.
Another form made from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 这是由同一词干构成的另一形式。

definition_zh: 坚持；坚决要求；坚称
definition_en: to say firmly that something must happen or is true, and refuse to give way
core_image: 一个人双手按在桌上，把同一句话再说一遍
scene: 饭馆里两个人抢着付账，谁也不肯退让。She insisted on paying for the meal herself.
sceneCN: 这里 insist 是「坚持要求」（第 1 个义项：坚决要求某事必须如此）；句意为她坚持自己付这顿饭钱。图中可辨识物件：账单、餐桌、钱包。

pos.zh: 动词：坚持；坚决要求；坚称

collocations.zh: 如果你一定要这样的话

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「坚持；坚决主张」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「坚持的；迫切的」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「坚持地」

senses.title: To demand firmly
senses.definition: to demand something firmly, refusing to accept a refusal
senses.definitionCN: 坚决要求某事，不接受拒绝
senses.example: He insisted on seeing the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚持要见经理。
senses.why: Insistere is to stand upon: a demand repeats until the ground no longer moves.
senses.whyCN: insistere 是「站上去」：要求反复提出，直到脚下的地面不再移动。

senses.title: To state firmly as true
senses.definition: to say something firmly and repeatedly as true, even when others doubt it
senses.definitionCN: 在他人怀疑时仍反复断言某事为真
senses.example: She insists that she never saw the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 她坚称自己从未见过那封信。
senses.why: A claim insisted upon is a claim the speaker will not withdraw under doubt.
senses.whyCN: 被 insist 的主张，是说话者在质疑下也不撤回的主张。

intro.en: Insist is Latin in- plus sistere "to stand": to keep standing on a point.
intro.cn: insist 是拉丁语 in- 加 sistere「站立」：坚持站在某一点上。

items.en: Sistere meant "to stand, to stop, to set in place".
items.cn: sistere 意为「站立、停住、安置」。

items.en: Insistere, from in- plus sistere, meant "to stand upon, to press upon".
items.cn: insistere 由 in- 加 sistere 构成，意为「站在上面、压在上面」。

items.en: In argument the image became to stand firm on a demand or a claim.
items.cn: 在辩论中，这一意象演变为在要求或主张上站稳脚跟。

items.en: French insister passed the verb to English in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 insister 在十六世纪把这个动词传入英语。

items.en: English insists on something, insists that something is true, or insists that someone act.
items.cn: 英语里可以说 insist on 某事、insist that 某事为真，或 insist that 某人去做。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of standing still; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of firm demand.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「站住」动词；近义组收表示坚决要求的动词。

entries.definition: To stand against something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抵抗」，即站在对面。

entries.definition: To keep standing, to continue stubbornly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坚持、持续」，强调一直不停。

entries.definition: To stand together, to be made up of.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「由……组成」。

entries.definition: To ask for something as a right, forcefully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「要求」，语气强硬，带有权利意味。

entries.definition: To keep saying that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「坚持声称」，多见于书面。

entries.definition: To keep doing something despite difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「执意坚持」，强调不顾阻力的持续。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use sistere, the verb of standing, and the patterns insist appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「站立」动词 sistere，以及 insist 的句型。

normal.en: Sistere is to stand: to insist is to stand on a point and not move off it.
normal.cn: sistere 是「站立」：insist 就是站在一点上不让步。

normal.en: Insist on takes an -ing form: insist on paying.
normal.cn: insist on 后接动名词：insist on paying。

normal.en: Insist that can also trigger a bare verb: they insist that he leave.
normal.cn: insist that 后也可接动词原形：they insist that he leave。

normal.en: Resist, persist and insist all involve taking a stand.
normal.cn: resist、persist、insist 都与「站定立场」有关。

normal.en: If you insist is the polite way to give way.
normal.cn: if you insist 是礼貌让步的说法。

abstract.en: Picture feet planted on one stone while the argument washes around them.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚牢牢踩在一块石上，争论在四周翻涌。

abstract.en: To insist is to make your position stronger than the pressure against it.
abstract.cn: 坚持就是让自己的位置强过压来的力量。

abstract.en: Firmness can protect another person's dignity, or simply one's own pride.
abstract.cn: 执着既能保护他人的体面，也可能只是护住自己的骄傲。

examples.en: They insisted on checking every detail.
examples.cn: 他们坚持要核对每一个细节。

examples.en: He insisted that the money was his.
examples.cn: 他坚称那笔钱是他的。

examples.en: If you insist, I will come with you.
examples.cn: 如果你一定要这样，我就陪你去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因塞斯特」——因他「塞」住不放，才叫坚持

root: 拉丁语 sistere「站立」加 in-「在上」构成 insistere「站上去、压上去」，在争论中引申为坚持主张；经法语 insister 于十六世纪入英语。同根词有 resist、persist、consist、exist。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: standing firm on a demand, and standing firm on a claim of fact.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：在要求上站稳立场，以及在事实主张上站稳立场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet planted on a single stone while the argument swirls round.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚踩定一块石头，争论在四周盘旋。

branches.en: THE TABLE: one diner insists on paying the whole bill.
branches.cn: 餐桌这条线：一位客人 insists on 付整笔账单。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a customer insists on seeing a manager.
branches.cn: 办公室这条线：顾客 insist on 见经理。

branches.en: THE COURT: a witness insists that the facts were as stated.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：证人坚称事实就是所述那样。

branches.en: THE FAMILY: people insist on being right within their own homes.
branches.cn: 家庭这条线：人在自己家里也要 insist 自己是对的。

branches.en: THE THREAD: both senses refuse to let the point be moved.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两个义项都拒绝让那个点被挪动。

intro.en: Insist is a Latin prefix on the verb for standing, and English keeps its Latin stem.
intro.cn: insist 是拉丁语前缀加「站立」动词，英语沿用其拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin sistere, insistere and the related stare are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sistere、insistere 以及相关的 stare 均有记录。

items.example: It marks standing upon a point.
The root of resist and persist.
items.exampleCN: resist 与 persist 的词根。
这是 insist 的直接来源。

items.example: It survives in all the English forms.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语各形式中留存。

definition_zh: 检查；视察；审视
definition_en: to look at something closely in order to judge its quality or find problems
core_image: 一双眼凑近齿轮，把每一道纹路都看一遍
scene: 车间里，质检员拿着记录板在机器之间慢慢走动。An engineer came to inspect the bridge after the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 inspect 是「检查、视察」（第 1 个义项：仔细查看以判断质量或发现问题）；句意为洪水过后有工程师来检查这座桥。图中可辨识物件：记录板、齿轮、手电筒。

pos.zh: 动词：检查；视察；审视

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「检查；视察」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「检查员；督察」
由 inspector 加后缀构成，义为「检查机构」

senses.title: To look at closely
senses.definition: to look at something carefully in order to judge it or find faults
senses.definitionCN: 为判断好坏或发现问题而仔细查看
senses.example: He inspected the tyres before the long drive.
senses.exampleCN: 长途出发前他检查了轮胎。
senses.why: Inspectare is to look over and over: the eye goes into the detail on purpose.
senses.whyCN: inspectare 是「反复查看」：眼睛有目的地深入细节。

senses.title: To visit officially to check
senses.definition: to visit a place officially and check that rules or standards are being kept
senses.definitionCN: 以官方身份到某地查看规章或标准是否被遵守
senses.example: Officials will inspect the school next month.
senses.exampleCN: 官员们下个月将来视察这所学校。
senses.why: When the state does the looking, inspection becomes a formal visit with authority behind it.
senses.whyCN: 当由国家来看时，inspection 就成了有权威支撑的正式到访。

intro.en: Inspect is Latin in- plus specere "to look": to look into something on purpose.
intro.cn: inspect 是拉丁语 in- 加 specere「看」：有目的地往里面看。

items.en: Specere meant "to look, observe", the root of spectacle, species and respect.
items.cn: specere 意为「看、观察」，是 spectacle、species、respect 的词根。

items.en: Inspectare, a frequentative of inspicere, meant "to look into, examine repeatedly".
items.cn: inspectare 是 inspicere 的反复形式，意为「往里看、反复查看」。

items.en: The noun inspectio was used of examining property and accounts.
items.cn: 名词 inspectio 用于察看财产与账目。

items.en: English adopted inspect in the seventeenth century for official and technical checks.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪采用 inspect，用于官方与技术的检查。

items.en: Modern use spans tyres, factories, bridges, and imported goods.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖轮胎、工厂、桥梁与进口货物。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of looking; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of checking.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「看」动词；近义组收其他表示查看的动词。

entries.definition: To look back at someone with esteem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「尊敬」，同根。

entries.definition: A person who watches an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观众」，同根。

entries.definition: To look up at someone with doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「怀疑」，同根。

entries.definition: To look at something in detail, often to test it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「检查、考查」，强调细究或测试。

entries.definition: To make sure something is correct or safe, quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「核对」，通常较快。

entries.definition: To look over a whole area or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「勘察、调查」，强调整体俯瞰。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use specere, the verb of looking, and the collocations the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「看」的动词 specere，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Specere is to look: to inspect is to look into something on purpose.
normal.cn: specere 是「看」：inspect 就是有目的地往里看。

normal.en: Respect, suspect and inspect are all ways of looking at someone.
normal.cn: respect、suspect、inspect 都是「看」的不同方式。

normal.en: An inspector inspects; an inspection is what he carries out.
normal.cn: inspector 负责 inspect，而 inspection 是他所做的检查。

normal.en: Inspect for damage means looking specifically for faults.
normal.cn: inspect for damage 意为专门查找破损。

normal.en: Goods are inspected before they leave the port.
normal.cn: 货物在离港前要接受查验。

abstract.en: Picture a magnifying glass over a seam: the eye decides what the hand will fix.
abstract.cn: 想象放大镜对准一道接缝：眼睛决定手该修哪里。

abstract.en: Inspection is trust replaced by evidence.
abstract.cn: 检查是用证据取代信任。

abstract.en: To inspect is to look with a question already in mind.
abstract.cn: 审视是带着问题去看。

examples.en: The car was inspected before it was sold.
examples.cn: 这辆车售出前接受过检查。

examples.en: Health officers inspect restaurants twice a year.
examples.cn: 卫生官员每年检查餐馆两次。

examples.en: She inspected the letter closely, looking for a date.
examples.cn: 她仔细查看那封信，想找日期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯派克特」——因要细细「看」，才去检查

root: 拉丁语 specere「看」加 in-「向内」构成 inspicere「往里看」，反复形式 inspectare 与名词 inspectio 经英语借入作 inspect；同根词有 respect、suspect、spectator、spectacle。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: looking closely at a thing, and looking over a place in an official role.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：仔细查看某物，以及以官方身份巡查某地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye brought close to a gear, following every groove.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛凑近齿轮，顺着每道沟纹看过去。

branches.en: THE WORKSHOP: goods are inspected before they are passed.
branches.cn: 车间这条线：货物在通过之前要受检。

branches.en: THE ROAD: tyres and brakes are inspected for safety.
branches.cn: 道路这条线：轮胎与刹车要检查是否安全。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: an official visit checks that standards are kept.
branches.cn: 学校这条线：官方到访核查标准是否被维持。

branches.en: THE PORT: customs officers inspect imported goods.
branches.cn: 港口这条线：海关人员查验进口货物。

branches.en: THE THREAD: both senses look with a judgement in mind, not for pleasure.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两种看都带着判断目的，而非为了欣赏。

intro.en: Inspect is a Latin prefix on the verb for looking, with a frequentative Latin stem.
intro.cn: inspect 是拉丁语前缀加「看」的动词，词干取反复形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin specere, inspicere, inspectare and inspectio are recorded, along with the related spectrum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 specere、inspicere、inspectare、inspectio 均有记录，还有相关的 spectrum。

items.example: It gives direction to the looking.
The root of spectacle and species.
items.exampleCN: spectacle 与 species 的词根。

items.example: It appears in inspector and respect.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 inspector 与 respect 中。

definition_zh: 居民；住户；（某地的）栖息动物
definition_en: a person or animal that lives in a particular place
core_image: 山脚下几间亮着灯的屋子，每一间里都有人在过日子
scene: 小镇只有一条街，店铺傍晚就早早关门。Every inhabitant of the island knows the ferry timetable by heart.
sceneCN: 这里 inhabitant 是「居民、住户」（第 1 个义项：居住在某地的人）；句意为岛上的每位居民都把渡船时刻表背得滚瓜烂熟。图中可辨识物件：屋顶、路灯、渡船。

pos.zh: 名词：居民；住户；栖息动物

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀还原，义为「居住于；栖息于」
由动词加过去分词构成，义为「有人居住的」
由动词加否定前缀构成，义为「无人居住的」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「可居住的」

senses.title: A person who lives in a place
senses.definition: a person who lives in a particular town, country, or building
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某个城镇、国家或建筑里的人
senses.example: Most inhabitants of the village work in the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 村里大多数居民在田里干活。
senses.why: In- "in" plus habitare "to dwell" gives a person who dwells inside a place.
senses.whyCN: in-「在内」加 habitare「居住」，得到的就是居住在某地之内的人。

senses.title: An animal that lives somewhere
senses.definition: an animal or plant that lives naturally in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 在某一地区自然生存的动物或植物
senses.example: Bats are the only inhabitants of the cave in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天蝙蝠是这处洞穴里唯一的栖息者。
senses.why: The same image applies to wild creatures: whoever dwells in a place is its inhabitant.
senses.whyCN: 同一意象也适用于野生生物：凡在某地安身者都是它的 inhabitant。

intro.en: Inhabitant comes from a Latin verb for dwelling, and its ending marks the one who does it.
intro.cn: inhabitant 来自拉丁语表示「居住」的动词，词尾标明动作的承担者。

items.en: Habere meant "to have, hold", and habitare grew from it with the sense "to hold a place, to dwell".
items.cn: habere 意为「拥有、持有」，habitare 由它演变而来，义为「占有某处、居住」。

items.en: The frequentative ending -itare gave habitare its repeated, settled flavour of living somewhere.
items.cn: 表示反复的 -itare 词尾让 habitare 带上「长期待在一处」的意味。

items.en: Old French inhabitant supplied the word to English with the -ant ending of a present participle.
items.cn: 古法语 inhabitant 以现在分词词尾 -ant 把这个词送进英语。

items.en: English adopted it in the late Middle Ages, chiefly in legal and geographical writing.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪晚期采用这个词，主要用于法律与地理文献。

items.en: It now covers animals and plants as easily as people, especially when a habitat is described.
items.cn: 如今它既指人，也常指动植物，尤其在描述栖息地时。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root of having and dwelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who live somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「拥有、居住」词根；近义组收表示「住在某地的人」的词。

entries.definition: The natural home of an animal or plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「栖息地」，指动植物的天然家园。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to live in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「居住于、栖息于」。

entries.definition: A settled way of behaving, from the same root of holding.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「习惯」，词根同为「持有」。

entries.definition: Someone who lives in a house or area, often formally recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「居民」，多用于正式登记语境。

entries.definition: A legal member of a state, not just someone living there.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公民」，指法律上的成员，而非仅居住者。

entries.definition: Someone born in a place, rather than merely living there.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「本地人」，强调出生于此。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build on habitare and on the phrases the word usually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子建立在 habitare 与这个词的常见搭配之上。

normal.en: Inhabit is to dwell in: an inhabitant is the one dwelling there.
normal.cn: inhabit 是「住在其中」：inhabitant 就是住在里面的人。

normal.en: Habit, habitat and inhabitant all come from a root meaning to hold.
normal.cn: habit、habitat、inhabitant 都出自表示「持有」的词根。

normal.en: Local inhabitants always know the shortest road.
normal.cn: 本地居民总知道最近的那条路。

normal.en: Writers speak of original inhabitants, meaning those who were there first.
normal.cn: 作者们说 original inhabitants，指最早住在那里的那些人。

normal.en: An uninhabited island has no inhabitants at all.
normal.cn: 无人居住的岛上一个居民也没有。

abstract.en: Picture a house with one lit window: the light is the sign that an inhabitant is inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋只亮着一扇窗的房子：那盏灯就是里面有住户的记号。

abstract.en: Inhabitant ties a creature to a place the way a name ties a person to a family.
abstract.cn: inhabitant 把生物与地点连起来，正如名字把人连到家族上。

abstract.en: Every place is defined as much by who dwells there as by what it looks like.
abstract.cn: 一个地方既由它的样子定义，也由住在那里的人定义。

examples.en: The town has fewer than two thousand inhabitants.
examples.cn: 这个镇子居民不到两千人。

examples.en: Foxes are common inhabitants of this forest.
examples.cn: 狐狸是这片森林常见的栖居者。

examples.en: The new road was welcomed by local inhabitants.
examples.cn: 新修的公路受到当地居民欢迎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因海比吞」——海边小屋有人住，因海而居成居民

root: 拉丁语 habitare「居住」来自 habere「拥有、持有」，反复词尾 -itare 表示长期待在一处；拉丁现在分词词干 inhabitant- 经古法语进入英语，-ant 标明「做这件事的人」。同根词有 habit、habitat、inhabit。

sensesIntro.en: One dwelling image serves both senses: a person who lives in a place, and an animal that lives there too.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共用同一个「居住」意象：住在某地的人，以及与之为邻的动物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house with a single lit window shows that someone dwells inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋只亮着一扇窗的房子说明里面住着人。

branches.en: THE HOUSE: the inhabitant is the one whose daily life fills a dwelling.
branches.cn: 房屋这条线：inhabitant 是日常生活填满一间屋子的那个人。

branches.en: THE TOWN: towns and countries are spoken of as having inhabitants rather than users.
branches.cn: 城镇这条线：说城镇与国家有 inhabitants，而不是使用它们的人。

branches.en: THE WILD: animals and plants are inhabitants of their habitat.
branches.cn: 野生这条线：动植物是它们栖息地的 inhabitants。

branches.en: THE CAVE: the word suits any dweller, including those that never build a house.
branches.cn: 洞穴这条线：这个词适用于任何栖居者，包括从不造房子的那些。

branches.en: THE PLACE: both senses bind a living thing firmly to one spot.
branches.cn: 地点线：两个义项都把生物牢牢绑在某一处。

intro.en: Inhabitant joins a Latin prefix, a Latin root of holding, and a participle ending that names the doer.
intro.cn: inhabitant 由拉丁语前缀、「持有」词根和标明动作承担者的分词词尾合成。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere, habitare and the participle inhabitans are recorded; only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere、habitare 及分词 inhabitans 均有记录，只有印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It places the dwelling inside a territory.
items.exampleCN: 它把居住放进某片地域之内。

items.example: The root also gives habit and able.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根还给出 habit 与 able。

items.example: It is the direct source of inhabit.
items.exampleCN: 它是 inhabit 的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the verb its settled, lasting sense.
items.exampleCN: 它让动词带上长久停留的意味。

items.example: It turns the verb into a name for a person.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成指人的名词。

items.example: The same root with a different ending.
A negative prefix marks the empty places.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀标出无人居住之处。

definition_zh: 继承（财产、地位或特征）；接手（遗留的问题）
definition_en: to receive money, property, or qualities from someone who has died or come before you
core_image: 老人留下的钥匙和账簿被交到下一代手里
scene: 祖父去世后，律师在书房里宣读遗嘱。She inherited the old farmhouse and all the land around it.
sceneCN: 这里 inherit 是「继承财产」（第 1 个义项：从去世的人那里接受钱财或产业）；句意为她继承了那座旧农舍以及周围所有土地。图中可辨识物件：遗嘱、钥匙、旧账簿。

pos.zh: 动词：继承；接手；遗传获得

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「遗产；继承」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「继承人」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「可继承的」
由本词加否定前缀构成，义为「剥夺继承权」

senses.title: To receive property from the dead
senses.definition: to receive money, property, or a title from someone after that person has died
senses.definitionCN: 在某人身故后接受其钱财、产业或头衔
senses.example: She inherited the house from her aunt.
senses.exampleCN: 她从姑妈那里继承了这所房子。
senses.why: In- "in" plus heres "heir" gave inhereditare, to put someone in the position of an heir.
senses.whyCN: in-「进入」加 heres「继承人」构成 inhereditare，意为把人放进继承人的位置。

senses.title: To take over a legacy of problems
senses.definition: to receive a situation, problem, or duty that someone else has left behind
senses.definitionCN: 接受别人留下的局面、问题或职责
senses.example: The new mayor inherited a city deep in debt.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长接手了一座负债累累的城市。
senses.why: What is passed down is not always wealth; an office or a mess can be handed over in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 传下来的不总是财富；职位或一团乱局也能以同样的方式移交。

senses.title: To get a quality through genes
senses.definition: to receive a physical or personal quality from one's parents or ancestors through genes
senses.definitionCN: 通过基因从父母或祖先那里获得身体或性格特征
senses.example: He inherited his mother's quick temper.
senses.exampleCN: 他遗传了母亲的急性子。
senses.why: Biology borrowed the legal image: parents hand down traits as families hand down land.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了法律上的意象：父母传下特征，正如家族传下土地。

intro.en: Inherit is a legal Latin word whose heir has become the everyday word for anything handed down.
intro.cn: inherit 本是一个法律拉丁词，其中的「继承人」如今成了泛指一切传承的日常语汇。

items.en: Heres meant "heir", a person who steps into another's property and standing.
items.cn: heres 意为「继承人」，指接替他人财产与地位的人。

items.en: Inhereditare, "to make an heir", built in- onto heres and was used of transferring an estate.
items.cn: inhereditare 意为「使成为继承人」，由 in- 加 heres 构成，用于转移产业。

items.en: Old French enheriter, "to make heir, to put in possession", shortened the form on its way to English.
items.cn: 古法语 enheriter 意为「立为继承人、使其占有」，在传入英语时形式缩短。

items.en: English took inherit in the fourteenth century, first in law, then in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入 inherit，先用于法律，后进入日常语言。

items.en: Since the nineteenth century it also covers traits passed through genes, not just property.
items.cn: 十九世纪以后，它也涵盖经基因传下的特征，而不只是财产。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the heir root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of receiving from someone else.
note.cn: 形近组保留「继承人」词根；近义组收其他表示「从他人处获得」的动词。

entries.definition: What is inherited, whether money or a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗产、遗传」，指被继承之物。

entries.definition: The person who inherits property or a title.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「继承人」，即继承财产或头衔的人。

entries.definition: The traditions and buildings a society passes down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗产、传统」，指社会传下的传统与建筑。

entries.definition: To take over an office or title after another person.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「继任」，多指接替职位或头衔。

entries.definition: To get something given to you, without the idea of a death.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收到」，不含继承的意味。

entries.definition: To gain something by your own effort or purchase.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得」，强调靠自己努力或购买。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real heir root and the phrases the word actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的「继承人」词根，以及这个词实际使用的搭配。

normal.en: Heres is heir: to inherit is to be put in the heir's place.
normal.cn: heres 就是「继承人」：inherit 就是被放进继承人位置。

normal.en: The same root gives heir, heritage and inheritance.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 heir、heritage、inheritance。

normal.en: You inherit money from a person, but you inherit a problem from a situation.
normal.cn: 钱是从人那里 inherit 来的，问题是从局面那里 inherit 来的。

normal.en: An inherited disease comes through the genes, not through a will.
normal.cn: inherited disease 是通过基因而非遗嘱得来的。

normal.en: A new manager often inherits the mistakes of the old one.
normal.cn: 新经理常常要接手前任犯下的错误。

abstract.en: Picture a key passed from an old hand to a young one: the door opens for the new owner.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙从老人的手交到年轻人的手里：门为新主人打开。

abstract.en: Inheritance is time travelling forward: the past arrives in the present as property, habit or illness.
abstract.cn: 继承是时间向前旅行：过去以财产、习惯或疾病的形式抵达现在。

abstract.en: You choose what to keep and what to change, but you cannot choose what you were handed.
abstract.cn: 你可以选择保留什么、改变什么，却无法选择自己被交到手里的东西。

examples.en: He inherited a small workshop from his father.
examples.cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一间小作坊。

examples.en: Children often inherit the habits of their parents.
examples.cn: 孩子常会遗传父母的习惯。

examples.en: The committee inherited an unfinished project.
examples.cn: 委员会接手了一个没做完的项目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因何丽特」——因何丽特得了遗产？因为她继承了老屋

root: 拉丁语 heres「继承人」加上 in- 构成 inhereditare「使成为继承人」，经古法语 enheriter 传入英语作 inherit；同根词有 heir、heritage、inheritance、heredity。十九世纪起又用于遗传学。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses share one image of handover: property after a death, a situation left by a predecessor, and traits passed through genes.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项共用一个「移交」意象：身后的财产、前任留下的局面，以及经基因传下的特征。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key and an account book pass from an old hand to a young one.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙与账簿从老人的手交到年轻人手里。

branches.en: THE WILL: property passes at death, and the law records who receives it.
branches.cn: 遗嘱这条线：财产在身故时转移，法律记录由谁接受。

branches.en: THE TITLE: names and offices are inherited as readily as land.
branches.cn: 头衔这条线：姓氏与职位和土地一样可以被继承。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a successor inherits whatever the predecessor left, good or bad.
branches.cn: 职位这条线：继任者接手前任留下的一切，无论好坏。

branches.en: THE BODY: genes hand down traits as families hand down land.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：基因传下特征，正如家族传下土地。

branches.en: THE THREAD: in every sense something arrives from the past and must be carried on.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项里都有东西从过去抵达，并须被延续。

intro.en: Inherit is a Latin prefix plus the Latin word for heir, reshaped in Old French and English.
intro.cn: inherit 是拉丁语前缀加拉丁语「继承人」一词，经古法语与英语改写而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres and inhereditare are recorded; the related heredity shows the same root in modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heres 与 inhereditare 均有记录，现代英语的 heredity 显示同一词根。

items.example: It places someone into the heir's position.
items.exampleCN: 它把人放进继承人的位置。

items.example: The noun is the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词义的核心。

items.meaning: to make an heir, to bequeath
items.example: The verb from which the word descends.
The stem was shortened in French.
items.exampleCN: 这一词干在法语中被缩短。

items.example: The root survives as a word on its own.
The learned form of the same root.
items.exampleCN: 这是同一词根的书面形式。

items.example: A negative prefix reverses the act.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把动作反了过来。

definition_zh: 最初的；开头的；（名词）首字母
definition_en: existing or happening at the beginning; also the first letter of a name
core_image: 长路尽头才有风景，但第一块路牌已经竖在脚下
scene: 报名表摊在桌上，需要填写姓名与地址。My initial reaction to the plan was cautious rather than hostile.
sceneCN: 这里 initial 是「最初的、第一反应」（第 1 个义项：发生在开头的）；句意为我对该计划的最初反应是谨慎而非敌意。图中可辨识物件：表格、钢笔、印章。

pos.zh: 形容词：最初的；开头的
名词：首字母（复数指姓名首字母）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「起初；最初」
同根动词，义为「发起；开始」
同根名词，义为「主动性；倡议」
由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「初始化」

senses.title: Happening at the beginning
senses.definition: existing or occurring at the start of a process, rather than later
senses.definitionCN: 存在于或发生在某一过程开头，而不是后来
senses.example: The initial results look promising.
senses.exampleCN: 初步结果看起来很有希望。
senses.why: Latin initium is a beginning; initial marks the door through which everything else must pass.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 initium 意为「开端」；initial 标出的就是一切后续都必须经过的那道门。

senses.title: The first letter of a name
senses.definition: the first letter of a word or name, often used as a short sign of identity
senses.definitionCN: 单词或姓名的第一个字母，常用来简短标明身份
senses.example: Please write your initials in the box.
senses.exampleCN: 请在方框里写上姓名的首字母。
senses.why: The beginning of a name stands for the whole person, as the beginning of a process stands for the process.
senses.whyCN: 名字的开头代表整个人，正如过程的开始代表整个过程。

intro.en: Initial comes straight from a Latin adjective of beginning, and its noun is simply initium, a start.
intro.cn: initial 直接来自拉丁语表示「开端」的形容词，其名词原形就是 initium（开始）。

items.en: The verb inire meant "to go in, to begin", built from in- and ire "to go".
items.cn: 动词 inire 意为「进入、开始」，由 in- 与 ire「走」构成。

items.en: From inire came initium, "a beginning", and the adjective initialis, "of the beginning".
items.cn: 由 inire 得到 initium「开端」与形容词 initialis「开端的」。

items.en: The church used initials for the opening letters of a name or a book long before printing.
items.cn: 早在印刷术之前，教会就用 initials 指名字或书的开头字母。

items.en: English borrowed initial in the sixteenth century, first as an adjective in learned prose.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借用 initial，最初作为形容词出现在学术文章中。

items.en: The noun initials became common with forms and signatures, and the adjective spread to costs and results.
items.cn: 名词 initials 随表格与签名普及，形容词则扩展到成本、结果等说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb for going in and beginning; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of coming first.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「进入、开始」的动词；近义组收表示「最先」的形容词。

entries.definition: The ability to act first, or a proposal that starts something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主动性、倡议」，指率先行动的能力或发起的方案。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to begin or to admit someone into a group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发起、准许加入」。

entries.definition: At first, in the opening stage.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「起初、最初」。

entries.definition: Existing from the very start and not copied.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的、原创的」，强调非复制。

entries.definition: Coming before all others, the plainest word for order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「第一的」，是最朴素的顺序词。

entries.definition: Coming before the main part, as a preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「初步的」，指正式部分前的准备。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb inire and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语动词 inire，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: inire is to go in: the beginning is the doorway you step through.
normal.cn: inire 是「走进去」：开始就是你要穿过的那道门。

normal.en: Initial, initiate, initiative and initially all share that doorway.
normal.cn: initial、initiate、initiative、initially 共享那道门。

normal.en: An initial reaction is the one you have before thinking twice.
normal.cn: initial reaction 是你再三思考之前就有的反应。

normal.en: Initial costs come before later savings.
normal.cn: 初期成本出现在后来节省之前。

normal.en: Your initials are the smallest version of your name.
normal.cn: 姓名首字母是名字最小的版本。

abstract.en: Picture the first signpost on a very long road: it is small, but it decides the direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一条极长的路上的第一块路牌：它很小，却决定了方向。

abstract.en: The initial moment is only a moment, yet it fixes what came after it.
abstract.cn: 最初的时刻只是一个瞬间，却固定了后来的一切。

abstract.en: Beginnings are agreements we make with the future before we know its terms.
abstract.cn: 开端是我们尚不知条款时与未来签下的约定。

examples.en: The initial plan had to be changed several times.
examples.cn: 最初的计划不得不改了好几次。

examples.en: Her initial answer was no, but she agreed later.
examples.cn: 她最初回答不，但后来同意了。

examples.en: Sign your initials at the bottom of each page.
examples.cn: 在每一页底部签上姓名的首字母。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一你手」——一伸手就抓住最初那段

root: 拉丁语 inire「走进、开始」= in-「向内」+ ire「走」，由它派生 initium「开端」和 initialis「开端的」；同根词有 initiate、initiative、initial、initially。initials 指姓名首字母。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the adjectival sense of what comes first, and the noun for the first letter of a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：形容词表示「最先的」，名词表示姓名开头的字母。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first signpost on a long road decides which way the whole journey goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：长路上的第一块路牌决定整段旅程的方向。

branches.en: THE START: initial describes whatever exists in the opening moments.
branches.cn: 开头这条线：initial 描述存在于最初时刻的东西。

branches.en: THE SOUNDING: an initial consonant is the one heard first in a word.
branches.cn: 发音这条线：initial consonant 指词首听到的那个辅音。

branches.en: THE SIGNATURE: initials stand in for a full name on forms and letters.
branches.cn: 签名这条线：initials 在表格和信件里代替全名。

branches.en: THE MARK: a single letter can mark ownership as clearly as a whole name.
branches.cn: 标记这条线：一个字母标出所属，效果与全名相同。

branches.en: THE THREAD: in both senses the first element stands for the whole.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两个义项里都是「最先的一小块」代表整体。

intro.en: Initial is a Latin adjective on a Latin verb of going in; English adds ordinary endings to build its family.
intro.cn: initial 是建立在拉丁语「走进」动词上的形容词，英语用普通词尾扩展成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ire, inire, initium and initialis are all recorded; only the Indo-European root of ire is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ire、inire、initium、initialis 均有记录，只有 ire 的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It marks the step through a doorway.
items.exampleCN: 它标出穿过门的那一步。

items.example: The verb also underlies exit and transit.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也构成 exit 与 transit。

items.example: The source of the noun for a beginning.
It forms initialis and English initial.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 initialis 与英语 initial。

definition_zh: 最初；起初；一开始
definition_en: at the beginning, especially when something changed later
core_image: 门刚推开的那一刻，屋子里还是空的
scene: 演出开始前，剧场里只亮着几盏工作灯。Initially the shop was a single room, but it now fills the whole building.
sceneCN: 这里 initially 是「最初、起初」（第 1 个义项：事情开始的时候，常暗示后来有变化）；句意为这家店最初只有一间屋子，现在却占满了整栋楼。图中可辨识物件：工作灯、卷帘门、招牌。

pos.zh: 副词：最初；起初；一开始

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀还原，义为「最初的；开头的」
同根动词，义为「发起；开始」
同根名词，义为「主动性；倡议」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「开始；入会」

senses.title: At the start of a process
senses.definition: at the beginning of a period or process, before later changes
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间或过程的开头，常与后来的变化相对
senses.example: Initially the job seemed easy.
senses.exampleCN: 起初这份工作看起来很容易。
senses.why: Latin initium is a beginning, and the adverb -ly simply places the statement at that point in time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 initium 意为「开端」，副词词尾 -ly 只是把陈述安放在那个时间点上。

senses.title: In the original plan or opinion
senses.definition: in the first version of a plan, estimate, or opinion, which was later revised
senses.definitionCN: 在最初版本的方案、估计或看法中，后经修改
senses.example: The meeting was initially set for Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 会议原本定在周一。
senses.why: What was first decided is described as initially decided, even after it has been changed.
senses.whyCN: 最初决定的事就用 initially 来叙述，即使它已被更改。

intro.en: Initially is the Latin adjective of beginning turned into an English adverb by a single suffix.
intro.cn: initially 是拉丁语「开端」形容词加上一个英语副词后缀变化而来。

items.en: Inire, "to go in, begin", came from in- plus ire "to go".
items.cn: inire 意为「进入、开始」，由 in- 与 ire「走」构成。

items.en: The noun initium meant "a beginning", and initialis described what belongs to it.
items.cn: 名词 initium 意为「开端」，initialis 描述属于开端的东西。

items.en: English took initial as an adjective in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 initial 作形容词。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly was added in the seventeenth century to mean "at first".
items.cn: 十七世纪加上副词词尾 -ly，表示「起初」。

items.en: Modern usage often implies a contrast: initially this, but later that.
items.cn: 现代用法常暗示对比：起初如此，后来那般。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the beginning root; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of early time.
note.cn: 形近组共享「开端」词根；近义组收表示早期时间的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective for what comes first.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的」。

entries.definition: To start something or admit someone into a group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发起、准许加入」。

entries.definition: The power to act first, or a starting proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主动性、倡议」。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for the opening moment, usually with a later contrast.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「起初」，最朴素的说法，常与后文对比。

entries.definition: In the first version or from the very source of something.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「原本」，强调最初的版本或本源。

entries.definition: Before anything else happened; neutral about later change.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「首先」，对后续变化不作暗示。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the beginning root and the sentence patterns this adverb really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「开端」词根，以及这个副词真实出现的句型。

normal.en: Initial plus -ly: the adjective of beginning turned into a time word.
normal.cn: initial 加 -ly：把「开端的」形容词变成时间副词。

normal.en: Initially usually comes with a but: it was like this, then it was not.
normal.cn: initially 常跟一个 but：本来如此，后来不是了。

normal.en: Things initially planned are often finally changed.
normal.cn: 最初计划的事情最后常常被改。

normal.en: She was initially reluctant, then agreed.
normal.cn: 她起初不情愿，后来同意了。

normal.en: The town was initially a fishing village.
normal.cn: 这个镇子最初是个渔村。

abstract.en: Picture the first page of a book before anyone has written the ending.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书的第一页，结尾还没有写。

abstract.en: Initially marks the moment when the future was still open.
abstract.cn: initially 标出未来还敞开着的那一刻。

abstract.en: Every final state was once an initial one.
abstract.cn: 每一种最终状态都曾是初始状态。

examples.en: Initially the plan met strong opposition.
examples.cn: 起初该计划遭到强烈反对。

examples.en: The building was initially used as a warehouse.
examples.cn: 这栋楼最初被用作仓库。

examples.en: Initially, nobody believed the story.
examples.cn: 起初没有人相信这件事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一你手里」——一开始就在你手里

root: initially 由拉丁语 initialis「开端的」（来自 inire「走进、开始」= in- + ire「走」）加英语副词后缀 -ly 构成；同根词有 initial、initiate、initiative、initiation。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: simply the time at the start, and the first version of a plan later revised.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：单纯指开头的时间，以及后来被改动的原定方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first page of a book, with the ending still unwritten.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本书的第一页，结尾尚未写就。

branches.en: THE TIME: initially places a statement at the opening of a period.
branches.cn: 时间这条线：initially 把陈述放在某段时间的开头。

branches.en: THE STATE: what was true at the start is reported without judgement.
branches.cn: 状态这条线：开头为真的情况被如实叙述，不作评价。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the first version of a plan is the one initially proposed.
branches.cn: 计划这条线：方案的第一版就是 initially 提出的那一版。

branches.en: THE ESTIMATE: figures initially given are often corrected later.
branches.cn: 估算这条线：最初给出的数字后来常被更正。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: the word quietly promises that something changed.
branches.cn: 对比这条线：这个词暗暗提示后来发生了变化。

intro.en: Initially is a Latin adjective of beginning with one English adverb suffix added.
intro.cn: initially 是一个拉丁语「开端」形容词加一个英语副词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ire, initium and initialis are recorded, so the word has a documented path.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ire、initium、initialis 均有记录，本词的发展路径有据可查。

items.example: It marks stepping through the opening.
items.exampleCN: 它标出迈过开端的那一步。

items.example: Also seen in exit and transit.
items.exampleCN: 在 exit 与 transit 中也能看到。
