items.example: The source of the beginning sense.

items.exampleCN: 这是 initial 背后的拉丁形容词。

items.example: It forms initially from the adjective.

definition_zh: 发起；开始实施；使初步了解；（经仪式）接纳为新成员
definition_en: to cause a process to begin, or to formally introduce someone into a group or skill
core_image: 第一块多米诺骨牌被手指轻轻推倒
scene: 会议室里摊开一叠项目提案，等待签字。The council voted to initiate a review of the whole system.
sceneCN: 这里 initiate 是「发起、开始实施」（第 1 个义项：促使某个过程开始）；句意为议会表决通过，启动对整个体系的审查。图中可辨识物件：提案、签字笔、桌灯。

pos.zh: 动词：发起；开始实施；引导入门；接纳为成员
名词：新加入者（多见于专业书面语）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「开始；入会仪式」
同根名词，义为「主动性；倡议」
同根形容词，义为「最初的」
由本词加表示人的后缀构成，义为「发起者」

senses.title: To start a process
senses.definition: to make a process, plan, or action begin
senses.definitionCN: 使某个过程、计划或行动开始
senses.example: The company initiated a new training programme.
senses.exampleCN: 公司启动了一项新的培训计划。
senses.why: Latin initiare is to begin, from initium "a beginning"; the verb names the act of opening the door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 initiare 意为「开始」，源自 initium「开端」；动词指的就是把门打开这一动作。

senses.title: To introduce someone to something new
senses.definition: to help someone learn about a subject or activity for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人第一次了解某学科或活动
senses.example: The course initiates students into the basics of law.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课引导学生进入法学的基础领域。
senses.why: To enter a new field is to be led through a beginning, so the verb means both to start and to bring someone to the start.
senses.whyCN: 进入新领域就是被带过一个开端，所以这个动词既表示开始，也表示把人领到起点。

senses.title: To admit someone by ceremony
senses.definition: to formally accept someone into a group, often with a special ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 正式接纳某人加入团体，常有专门仪式
senses.example: New members are initiated at the spring meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 新成员在春季会议上被正式接纳。
senses.why: Secret societies and clubs turned the doorway image into a real rite of passage.
senses.whyCN: 秘密社团与俱乐部把「门」的意象变成了真实的入会仪式。

intro.en: Initiate is the Latin verb of beginning that English borrowed for plans, lessons and ceremonies alike.
intro.cn: initiate 是拉丁语表示「开始」的动词，英语用它兼指计划、入门与仪式。

items.en: Inire, from in- and ire "to go", meant "to go in, to begin".
items.cn: inire 由 in- 与 ire「走」构成，意为「进入、开始」。

items.en: Initium, "a beginning", and the verb initiare, "to begin or admit", followed from it.
items.cn: 由它派生出 initium「开端」以及动词 initiare「开始、接纳」。

items.en: In religious use initiare meant to admit someone to the mysteries, a sacred beginning.
items.cn: 在宗教用法中 initiare 指让人进入秘仪，是一种神圣的开端。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the seventeenth century for starting actions and for formal admission.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪采用这个动词，用于发起行动与正式纳新。

items.en: Business and law now use it for launching projects and proceedings.
items.cn: 如今商业与法律领域用它表示启动项目与程序。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the root of beginning; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of starting.
note.cn: 形近组共享「开端」词根；近义组收表示「开始」的动词。

entries.definition: A proposal that starts action, or the drive to act first.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「倡议、主动性」。

entries.definition: The adjective for what comes first.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的」。

entries.definition: The act of starting, or a ceremony of admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「开始、入会仪式」。

entries.definition: To start something big with publicity, like a product or a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推出、发射」，多指有声势地启动产品或船只。

entries.definition: The most general verb for starting anything.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「开始」，最通用的说法。

entries.definition: To cause something to happen suddenly, like a reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引发」，强调突然触发反应。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb of beginning and the phrases the word routinely takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁语「开始」动词，以及这个词常用的搭配。

normal.en: Initium is a beginning: to initiate is to push the first domino.
normal.cn: initium 是开端：initiate 就是推倒第一块骨牌。

normal.en: The noun initiative keeps the same root: the will to begin.
normal.cn: 名词 initiative 同根，指「开始的意愿」。

normal.en: Companies initiate projects, courts initiate proceedings.
normal.cn: 公司发起项目，法院启动程序。

normal.en: Be initiated into a club means to be let in through its door.
normal.cn: be initiated into a club 指被放进俱乐部的大门。

normal.en: An initiator is whoever acts first.
normal.cn: initiator 就是最先行动的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture a finger on the first domino: everything after that is consequence.
abstract.cn: 想象手指按在第一块骨牌上：其后的一切都是后果。

abstract.en: Initiate is a choice, not an accident: someone decides the beginning will happen.
abstract.cn: initiate 是一种选择而非偶然：有人决定让开始发生。

abstract.en: Every beginning costs something, which is why starting is harder than continuing.
abstract.cn: 每个开始都有代价，这正是开始比继续更难的原因。

examples.en: The government initiated talks with the union.
examples.cn: 政府启动了与工会的谈判。

examples.en: Senior students initiate the newcomers into college life.
examples.cn: 高年级学生引导新生适应大学生活。

examples.en: The club initiated ten new members last month.
examples.cn: 俱乐部上个月正式接纳了十名新成员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一你谁特」——一开始就问你是谁，然后让你入门

root: 拉丁语 inire「走进、开始」（in- + ire「走」）派生 initium「开端」与 initiare「开始、接纳」；英语十七世纪借入 initiate。同根词：initial、initially、initiative、initiation。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses all show a doorway being opened: a process begins, a learner is led in, a member is formally admitted.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在展示一扇被打开的门：过程开始、学习者被领进门、成员被正式接纳。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tips the first domino and the whole line falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指推倒第一块骨牌，整排随之倒下。

branches.en: THE PROJECT: a plan or policy is initiated when someone starts it.
branches.cn: 项目这条线：方案或政策在有人启动它时被 initiate。

branches.en: THE COURT: legal action is initiated by the party who files first.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：诉讼由先提起诉讼的一方 initiate。

branches.en: THE LESSON: a teacher initiates beginners into a subject.
branches.cn: 课堂这条线：老师把初学者领进一门学科。

branches.en: THE RITE: a club initiates new members with a ceremony.
branches.cn: 仪式这条线：俱乐部用仪式接纳新成员。

branches.en: THE THREAD: every sense puts someone or something on the inside of a beginning.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项都把人或事放到了开端的里面。

intro.en: Initiate is the Latin verb of beginning, keeping its Latin verb ending in English.
intro.cn: initiate 是拉丁语「开始」动词，英语保留了它的动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin inire, initium and initiare are recorded, all built on the verb ire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inire、initium、initiare 均有记录，都建立在动词 ire 上。

items.example: It marks entering the new state.
The base of the whole family.

items.exampleCN: 这是 initiate 的直接来源。

items.example: It carries the Latin verb ending into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁动词词尾带进英语。

definition_zh: 主动性；主动权；倡议；新方案
definition_en: the ability or willingness to act first without being told, or a new plan put forward to solve something
core_image: 没人下令，一个人先站起来走了出去
scene: 会上人人低头看笔记，没有人愿意开口。To her credit, she took the initiative and wrote to the supplier herself.
sceneCN: 这里 initiative 是「主动性、主动权」（第 1 个义项：不必别人吩咐就先行行动的能力）；句意为值得称道的是，她主动出击，自己给供应商写了信。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、笔记本、信纸。

pos.zh: 名词：主动性；主动权；倡议；新方案

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「发起；开始」
同根形容词，义为「最初的」
同根名词，义为「发起者」
同根名词，义为「开始；入会」

senses.title: The will to act first
senses.definition: the ability and willingness to decide and act before others do, without being ordered
senses.definitionCN: 在他人之前自行决定并行动的能力与意愿
senses.example: Employers value staff who show initiative.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主看重有主动性的员工。
senses.why: Initialis describes what belongs to a beginning; initiative is the quality of making that beginning yourself.
senses.whyCN: initialis 描述属于开端的东西；initiative 则是自己做出这个开端的能力。

senses.title: A new plan put forward
senses.definition: a new plan or programme, often by a government or group, to solve a problem
senses.definitionCN: 由政府或团体提出的解决某问题的新方案或计划
senses.example: The city launched an initiative to plant more trees.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市发起了一项植树倡议。
senses.why: When a group makes the first move in public, the beginning itself is put on the table as a scheme.
senses.whyCN: 当团体公开迈出第一步，这个开端本身就作为方案摆上台面。

intro.en: Initiative is a modern noun built on the Latin adjective of beginning: the faculty of making beginnings.
intro.cn: initiative 是建立在拉丁语「开端」形容词上的现代名词，指「做出开端的能力」。

items.en: Initium, from inire "to go in", meant "a beginning"; initialis described what belongs to a beginning.
items.cn: initium 来自 inire「进入」，意为「开端」；initialis 描述属于开端的东西。

items.en: French gave the word its political form, initiative, for the right to propose a law.
items.cn: 法语赋予这个词政治形态 initiative，指提出法案的权利。

items.en: English adopted initiative in the eighteenth century in political writing about the power to propose.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪引入 initiative，用于讨论提案权的政治文献。

items.en: By the nineteenth century it also named personal drive, the habit of acting without orders.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，它也指个人干劲，即不待吩咐就行动的作风。

items.en: The twentieth century added the sense of a public campaign or programme.
items.cn: 二十世纪又增添了公共倡议或项目的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the beginning root; the near-meaning group gathers words for drive and for plans.
note.cn: 形近组共享「开端」词根；近义组收表示干劲与方案的词。

entries.definition: To start a process or admit someone to a group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发起、接纳」。

entries.definition: The adjective for what comes first.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最初的」。

entries.definition: At first, before later changes.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「起初」。

entries.definition: Inner energy that pushes a person to work hard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「干劲」，指推动人努力的内在能量。

entries.definition: A plan formally suggested for others to consider.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提议」，指正式提出供人考虑的计划。

entries.definition: Boldness in starting new things, or a business venture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进取心、事业」，兼指敢闯的精神与经营项目。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the beginning root and the fixed phrases the noun appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用「开端」词根，以及这个名词的固定搭配。

normal.en: Take the initiative is the phrase to learn: nobody asks you, you move.
normal.cn: 先记住 take the initiative：没人叫你，你自己先动。

normal.en: On your own initiative means the idea was yours.
normal.cn: on your own initiative 意为这事是你自己想出来的。

normal.en: A peace initiative puts a first plan on the table.
normal.cn: a peace initiative 是把第一份方案摆上桌面。

normal.en: Initiate starts the action; initiative names the spirit behind it.
normal.cn: initiate 是开始的动作，initiative 是动作背后的精神。

normal.en: A colleague who shows initiative rarely waits to be told.
normal.cn: 表现出主动性的同事很少等着被吩咐。

abstract.en: Picture one hand raised in a room where every other hand stays down.
abstract.cn: 想象在一个所有人都垂着手的房间里，有一只手举了起来。

abstract.en: Initiative is the private decision that becomes a public beginning.
abstract.cn: 主动性是私人决定，最终成为公共的开端。

abstract.en: Energy that begins inside a person becomes motion that others can follow.
abstract.cn: 从一个人内部开始的能量，会变成别人能跟随的运动。

examples.en: She took the initiative and called the client first.
examples.cn: 她主动出击，先给客户打了电话。

examples.en: He joined the project on his own initiative.
examples.cn: 他凭自己的主动加入了该项目。

examples.en: The school started an initiative to cut food waste.
examples.cn: 学校发起了一项减少食物浪费的倡议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一你谁提五」——一开始你自己提出来，就是主动性

root: initiative 源出拉丁语 initialis「开端的」（来自 initium「开端」，再上溯 inire「进入」）；法语 initiative 指提案权，十八世纪进入英语，十九世纪引申为个人干劲，二十世纪又指公共倡议。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: the inner drive to act first, and the public plan that results from it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：先行行动的内在动力，以及由它产生的公开方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand goes up in a room where all other hands stay down.
core.cn: 核心意象：满屋子的手都垂着，只有一只手举了起来。

branches.en: THE PERSON: initiative is a habit of acting before being asked.
branches.cn: 个人这条线：initiative 是无需被要求就行动的作风。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: to have the initiative is to be the side that moves first.
branches.cn: 权利这条线：拥有 initiative 就是先行动的一方。

branches.en: THE CITY: a public initiative is a launched programme with a goal.
branches.cn: 城市这条线：公共 initiative 是带目标启动的项目。

branches.en: THE TABLE: the plan is placed before others for approval.
branches.cn: 桌面这条线：方案被摆到别人面前等待通过。

branches.en: THE THREAD: the private decision and the public plan are two ends of one beginning.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：私人决定与公开方案是同一个开端的两端。

intro.en: Initiative is a Latin beginning adjective with a suffix that names a quality or tendency.
intro.cn: initiative 是拉丁语「开端」形容词加表示性质与倾向的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin initium and initialis are recorded; the noun initiative itself is a later French and English formation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 initium 与 initialis 有记录；名词 initiative 本身是较晚的法语与英语构形。

items.example: The sense of beginning runs through the word.

items.exampleCN: 这是名词背后的形容词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a name for a quality.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表示性质的名词。

items.example: The plain adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族中最朴素的形容词。

definition_zh: 注射；注射剂；（资金的）注入
definition_en: the act of putting a liquid medicine into the body with a needle, or the act of adding money or energy to something
core_image: 一支针筒把药液推进皮肤下面
scene: 诊室里护士正在消毒棉球旁准备器械。The child cried for a moment, then forgot the injection entirely.
sceneCN: 这里 injection 是「注射」（第 1 个义项：用针把药液送入体内）；句意为孩子哭了一会儿，随后就完全忘了打针这回事。图中可辨识物件：针筒、棉球、消毒盘。

pos.zh: 名词：注射；注射剂；注入

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原，义为「注射；注入」
由动词加表示工具的后缀构成，义为「注射器」
由动词加后缀构成，义为「可注射的」

senses.title: Medicine put in by needle
senses.definition: the act of forcing liquid medicine into the body through a needle or tube
senses.definitionCN: 用针或导管把药液压入体内的行为
senses.example: The nurse gave him an injection in the arm.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在他胳膊上打了一针。
senses.why: In- "into" plus iacere "to throw" gives the picture of liquid thrown into the body.
senses.whyCN: in-「向内」加 iacere「投掷」，构成把液体投进身体的画面。

senses.title: The medicine itself
senses.definition: a measured amount of liquid medicine prepared to be injected
senses.definitionCN: 预先配好准备用于注射的一份药液
senses.example: The doctor prepared an injection of insulin.
senses.exampleCN: 医生准备了一针胰岛素。
senses.why: The act and the dose share one name, as with many medical procedures.
senses.whyCN: 动作与剂量共用一个名称，这在医疗术语中很常见。

senses.title: Money or energy added
senses.definition: the addition of money, effort, or liveliness to something that needs it
senses.definitionCN: 向欠缺之处补充金钱、努力或活力
senses.example: The cash injection saved the factory.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔资金注入救了这家工厂。
senses.why: Anything pushed forcibly into a weakened system is injected, whether serum or money.
senses.whyCN: 凡是强行推进虚弱体系的东西都算注入，无论血清还是资金。

intro.en: Injection joins a Latin prefix meaning into with a Latin verb meaning to throw.
intro.cn: injection 把拉丁语表示「向内」的前缀与表示「投掷」的动词结合起来。

items.en: Iacere meant "to throw, hurl", and it produced many verbs of projecting and sending.
items.cn: iacere 意为「投掷」，构成了许多表示投射与发送的动词。

items.en: Inicere, from in- plus iacere, meant "to throw in, insert".
items.cn: inicere 由 in- 加 iacere 构成，意为「投入、插入」。

items.en: The noun iniectio could already mean a casting in, including of fluids.
items.cn: 名词 iniectio 当时已可表示「投入」，包括液体的注入。

items.en: French injection carried the medical sense of introducing fluids.
items.cn: 法语 injection 带有引入液体的医学含义。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century; syringes made the medical sense dominant later.
items.cn: 英语十五世纪借入该词，后来注射器的普及使医学义成为主导。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin verb of throwing; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of putting things in.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「投掷」动词；近义组收其他「放入」的说法。

entries.definition: To throw someone or something out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「弹出、驱逐」，即向外抛出。

entries.definition: To throw forward, literally or in planning.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投射、规划」，即向前抛出。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to force liquid or money in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「注射、注入」。

entries.definition: A preparation given to create immunity, often by injection.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「疫苗」，常通过注射接种。

entries.definition: A measured quantity of medicine taken at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一剂」，指一次服用的药量。

entries.definition: Slow introduction of liquid into the body, or of new life into something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「输液、注入」，强调缓慢流入。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use iacere, the verb of throwing, and the phrases the word occurs in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用表示投掷的 iacere，以及这个词出现的搭配。

normal.en: iacere is to throw: an injection throws medicine in through a needle.
normal.cn: iacere 是「投掷」：injection 是用针把药投进去。

normal.en: Project, eject and inject all throw in different directions.
normal.cn: project、eject、inject 都是朝不同方向投掷。

normal.en: You are given an injection; you do not give it to yourself.
normal.cn: 你是被 give an injection，不会自己给自己打。

normal.en: A cash injection throws money into a struggling business.
normal.cn: cash injection 是把钱投进挣扎中的企业。

normal.en: An injector is the tool; an injection is the act.
normal.cn: injector 是工具，injection 是动作。

abstract.en: Picture liquid meeting the skin's resistance, then passing through it.
abstract.cn: 想象液体遇上皮肤的阻力，然后穿了过去。

abstract.en: Injection is a short, sharp entrance: something outside is forced inside.
abstract.cn: 注射是一次短促的进入：外面的东西被强行送到里面。

abstract.en: A system that is failing can be revived by a sudden push from outside.
abstract.cn: 一个衰败的系统可以被外界突然的一推救活。

examples.en: The doctor gave her an injection to ease the pain.
examples.cn: 医生给她打了一针以减轻疼痛。

examples.en: Two injections a day were needed at first.
examples.cn: 起初每天需要打两针。

examples.en: The company received a large cash injection from investors.
examples.cn: 公司从投资者那里获得了一大笔资金注入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因杰克逊」——因杰克逊医生打了一针，病就好了

root: 拉丁语 iacere「投掷」加 in-「向内」构成 inicere「投入」，名词 iniectio 经法语 injection 进入英语，十五世纪已有记录；同根词有 eject、project、reject、inject。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses come from one image of forcing something in: the act of injecting, the dose injected, and money or energy pushed into a system.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项出自同一个「强行送入」的意象：注射的动作、被注入的药剂，以及注入系统的金钱或活力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a syringe pushes liquid through the skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：针筒把液体推进皮肤。

branches.en: THE ACT: an injection is the moment of forcing liquid in.
branches.cn: 动作这条线：injection 是强行送入液体的那一刻。

branches.en: THE DOSE: the prepared amount is named with the same word.
branches.cn: 剂量这条线：备好的那份药液用同一个词称呼。

branches.en: THE MONEY: cash is injected into a business that needs it.
branches.cn: 资金这条线：钱被注入需要它的企业。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: new energy can be injected into a dull event.
branches.cn: 精神这条线：活力也能被注入沉闷的活动。

branches.en: THE THREAD: something from outside enters quickly and changes the state inside.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：外面的东西迅速进入并改变内部状态。

intro.en: Injection is a Latin prefix plus a Latin throwing verb, with a noun ending added along the way.
intro.cn: injection 由拉丁语前缀与「投掷」动词构成，中途加上名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin iacere, inicere and iniectio are recorded; the noun form came through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iacere、inicere、iniectio 均有记录，名词形式经法语传入。

items.example: It sets the direction of the throw.
The root also gives eject and project.
items.exampleCN: 这一词根还给出 eject 与 project。
这是名词背后的复合动词。

definition_zh: 使受伤；损害（名誉、感情等）
definition_en: to hurt a person or animal physically, or to damage something such as a reputation
core_image: 奔跑的人踩滑了脚，重重摔在石阶上
scene: 雨后的石阶又湿又滑，走路的人都放慢了脚步。Two players were injured in the final minutes of the match.
sceneCN: 这里 injure 是「使受伤」（第 1 个义项：造成身体上的损伤）；句意为比赛最后几分钟里有两名球员受伤。图中可辨识物件：石阶、球门、担架。

pos.zh: 动词：使受伤；损害

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「伤害；受伤处」
由过去分词转化，义为「受伤的」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「有害的；造成伤害的」

senses.title: To hurt the body
senses.definition: to cause physical harm to a person or animal, often by accident
senses.definitionCN: 使人和动物身体受到损伤，多出于意外
senses.example: He injured his knee while climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 他爬山时伤了膝盖。
senses.why: Latin iniuria is a wrong, built from in- "not" and ius "right"; to injure is to do someone a wrong in the body.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 iniuria 意为「不公」，由 in-「非」与 ius「法」构成；injure 就是在身体上对人做不义之事。

senses.title: To damage a reputation or feeling
senses.definition: to harm something abstract such as a reputation, an interest, or someone's pride
senses.definitionCN: 损害名誉、利益或他人自尊等抽象事物
senses.example: The rumour injured her good name.
senses.exampleCN: 这则谣言损害了她的好名声。
senses.why: The old legal sense survives here: a wrong need not leave a visible wound to count as injury.
senses.whyCN: 古老的法律义在此留存：不义之事不必留下可见的伤口，也算伤害。

intro.en: Injure began as a legal word about wrongs, and only later narrowed towards bodily harm.
intro.cn: injure 最初是关于「不义」的法律词，后来才收窄到身体伤害。

items.en: Ius meant "right, law", the basis of justice and injury alike.
items.cn: ius 意为「法、权利」，justice 与 injury 都以此为基础。

items.en: Iniuria, from in- "not" plus ius, meant "injustice, a wrong done to someone".
items.cn: iniuria 由 in-「非」加 ius 构成，意为「不义、对他人施加的侵害」。

items.en: Old French injurier meant "to wrong, to insult or harm", with no physical limit.
items.cn: 古法语 injurier 意为「侵害、侮辱或伤害」，并不限于身体。

items.en: English injure first meant to wrong or insult someone, in law and in speech.
items.cn: 英语 injure 最初指在法律或言语上侵害、侮辱他人。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the bodily sense grew dominant, while damage to reputation remained.
items.cn: 十七世纪起身体受伤的义项成为主流，损害名誉的用法则保留下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin word for right and wrong; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of causing harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「法、权利」一词；近义组收表示「造成伤害」的动词。

entries.definition: The harm itself, or a place on the body that hurts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤害、伤处」。

entries.definition: Unfairness, a wrong that is not physical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不公」，指非身体的侵害。

entries.definition: Causing harm, often to health or interests.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的」，多指对健康或利益。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for pain, physical or emotional.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使疼痛、伤心」，日常用语，兼指身心。

entries.definition: To cut or break the body, typically in fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使受伤」，多指打斗中造成的创口。

entries.definition: To harm things rather than people, or to harm partly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「损坏」，多用于物，且指部分损害。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the legal root of ius and the phrases the word takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 ius 这一法律词根，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Iniuria is a wrong: injure is to do someone a wrong in the body.
normal.cn: iniuria 是「不义」：injure 是在身体上对人行不义。

normal.en: Justice and injury share the root ius, law and right.
normal.cn: justice 与 injury 共享词根 ius，即「法、权利」。

normal.en: Players are injured; reputations can be injured too.
normal.cn: 球员会受伤，名誉也会被损害。

normal.en: The injured, used as a plural noun, means the people who were hurt.
normal.cn: the injured 作复数名词，指受伤的人们。

normal.en: An injurious habit is one that harms your health.
normal.cn: injurious habit 是损害健康的习惯。

abstract.en: Picture a straight line broken on one side: the wrong is the gap.
abstract.cn: 想象一条直线被一侧破开：那道缺口就是不义。

abstract.en: An injury is a violation before it is a wound.
abstract.cn: 伤害首先是「违犯」，然后才是伤口。

abstract.en: What harms the body and what harms the name spring from the same idea of treating a person wrongly.
abstract.cn: 伤身与伤名都出自同一观念：错待一个人。

examples.en: She injured her ankle during training.
examples.cn: 她在训练中伤了脚踝。

examples.en: Three workers were injured in the accident.
examples.cn: 三名工人在事故中受伤。

examples.en: Such careless words may injure your reputation.
examples.cn: 这样轻率的话可能损害你的名誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因之」——因而受了伤，因之而伤

root: 拉丁语 ius「法、权利」加否定前缀构成 iniuria「不义」，动词 iniuriare 经古法语 injurier 变为英语 injure；同根词有 injury、injurious、justice、injustice。十七世纪后以「身体受伤」为主义。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: harm done to a body, and harm done to something as abstract as a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：对身体造成的损伤，以及对名誉这类抽象之物的损害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line of fair treatment is broken on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条公平相待的直线被一侧破开。

branches.en: THE BODY: an accident or blow injures a limb or an organ.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：事故或打击伤到肢体或器官。

branches.en: THE GAME: players are injured in sport far more often than in daily life.
branches.cn: 赛场这条线：球员在运动中受伤远比日常生活中频繁。

branches.en: THE NAME: careless words injure a reputation without leaving a mark.
branches.cn: 名誉这条线：轻率的话损害名誉而不留痕迹。

branches.en: THE FEELING: pride and trust can be injured by the same wrong.
branches.cn: 情感这条线：自尊与信任也会被同一种不义伤到。

branches.en: THE THREAD: both senses come from the old legal idea of doing someone a wrong.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两个义项都源自「对他人行不义」这一古老法律观念。

intro.en: Injure is a negative Latin prefix on the word for law and right, softened by Old French.
intro.cn: injure 是「法、权利」一词加拉丁否定前缀，再经古法语软化而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius, iniuria and iniuriari are recorded, along with the related iustitia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ius、iniuria、iniuriari 均有记录，还有相关的 iustitia。

The root of justice and injury alike.

definition_zh: 伤害；受伤；伤处；（对名誉等的）损害
definition_en: physical harm done to a person or animal, or a place on the body that has been hurt
core_image: 膝盖上一道贴了胶布的伤口
scene: 球场边的长椅上，队医正低头查看球员的小腿。A knee injury kept him out of the game for two months.
sceneCN: 这里 injury 是「伤、伤病」（第 1 个义项：对身体造成的损伤）；句意为膝伤让他两个月没能上场。图中可辨识物件：长椅、药箱、冰袋。

pos.zh: 名词：伤害；受伤处；损害

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀还原，义为「使受伤；损害」
由动词过去分词构成，义为「受伤的」
由本词同根加后缀构成，义为「有害的」

senses.title: Harm done to the body
senses.definition: physical harm done to a person or animal, especially in an accident or sport
senses.definitionCN: 在事故或运动中对人或动物造成的身体损伤
senses.example: The fall caused a minor injury to his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 这一跤让他的胳膊受了轻伤。
senses.why: Injury is the noun of iniuria, a wrong; the first wrong the body knows is a break in its wholeness.
senses.whyCN: injury 是 iniuria（不义）的名词形式；身体最先感到的不义，就是完整被打破。

senses.title: A place that hurts
senses.definition: a particular place on the body that has been hurt, or the wound itself
senses.definitionCN: 身体上受伤的部位或创口本身
senses.example: The nurse cleaned the injury carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 护士仔细清洗了伤口。
senses.why: The whole harm and the visible spot it leaves are named with one word.
senses.whyCN: 整体的损害与它留下的可见部位共用同一个词。

senses.title: Damage to reputation or rights
senses.definition: harm done to a reputation, feeling, or legal right rather than to the body
senses.definitionCN: 对名誉、情感或法律权利的损害，而非身体的
senses.example: He sued the paper for injury to his reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 他起诉该报损害了他的名誉。
senses.why: Law keeps the oldest sense alive: an injury is any wrong suffered, not only a wound.
senses.whyCN: 法律保留了最古老的义项：injury 是任何受到的不义，而不只是伤口。

intro.en: Injury is the noun of a legal wrong that came to mean a physical hurt.
intro.cn: injury 原本指法律上的不义，后来才指身体的伤害。

items.en: Ius meant "right, law", the source of iustitia and iniuria alike.
items.cn: ius 意为「权利、法」，是 iustitia 与 iniuria 共同的来源。

items.en: Iniuria, "injustice", was formed with the negative in-; the adjective iniurius described what was wrongful or harmful.
items.cn: iniuria 以否定前缀 in- 构成，意为「不义」；形容词 iniurius 指不义或有害的。

items.en: Late Latin injuria narrowed towards damage and insult in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中 injuria 在日常用语里向「损害、侮辱」收窄。

items.en: Old French injurie passed the word to English with both the moral and the physical senses.
items.cn: 古法语 injurie 把词传给英语，道德义与身体义并存。

items.en: Sports and medicine fixed the bodily sense, while law kept the broader one.
items.cn: 体育与医学固定了身体义，法律则保留了更宽的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the root of law and wrong; the near-meaning group gathers other words for hurts and wounds.
note.cn: 形近组保留「法、不义」词根；近义组收其他表示伤痛与伤口的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hurt or wrong someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使受伤、侵害」。

entries.definition: A wrong that is moral rather than physical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不公」，指道德而非身体的侵害。

entries.definition: Harmful, especially to health.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有害的」，多指损害健康。

entries.definition: A cut or break in the body, often from a weapon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤口」，多指武器造成的创口。

entries.definition: Damage of any kind, to people or things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「损害」，范围最宽，可指人或物。

entries.definition: Pain or damage, often emotional as well as physical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「伤痛」，也常指情感伤害。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the legal root of ius and the collocations the noun takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 ius 这一法律词根，以及这个名词的搭配。

normal.en: Iniuria is a wrong: an injury was first a wrong before it was a wound.
normal.cn: iniuria 是「不义」：injury 先是侵害，后才是伤口。

normal.en: You suffer an injury but you receive treatment for it.
normal.cn: 你是 suffer an injury，然后接受治疗。

normal.en: Injury time in football replaces the minutes lost to stoppages.
normal.cn: 足球里的 injury time 补上因停顿而损失的时间。

normal.en: Justice and injury share the root ius, law and right.
normal.cn: justice 与 injury 共享词根 ius，即「法、权利」。

normal.en: A knee injury can end a season early.
normal.cn: 膝伤可能让一个赛季提前结束。

abstract.en: Picture a fair line broken on one side: the break is the injury.
abstract.cn: 想象一条公平的线被一侧破开：那道断裂就是伤害。

abstract.en: An injury is a subtraction: something that belonged to you is taken away.
abstract.cn: 伤害是一种减法：属于你的东西被拿走了。

abstract.en: Healing is not erasing: the body remembers where the injury was.
abstract.cn: 愈合不是抹除：身体记得伤在哪里。

examples.en: He missed the season because of a back injury.
examples.cn: 他因背伤错过了整个赛季。

examples.en: The injury healed slowly but completely.
examples.cn: 伤口愈合得慢，但最后还是痊愈了。

examples.en: The court recognised the injury to her good name.
examples.cn: 法院认可她的名誉受到了损害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因哲瑞」——因哲瑞受了伤，才明白健康可贵

root: 拉丁语 ius「法、权利」加否定前缀成 iniuria「不义」，形容词 iniurius 指不义或有害；晚期拉丁语 injuria 转向「损害」，经古法语 injurie 进入英语。同根词：injure、injurious、justice、injustice。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the harm as a whole, the hurt spot on the body, and the older legal wrong against a name or right.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：整体的损害、身体上的伤处，以及针对名誉或权利的古老法律义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fair line is broken on one side, leaving a gap that hurts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条公平的线被一侧破开，留下疼痛的缺口。

branches.en: THE ACCIDENT: most injuries happen suddenly, in traffic, at work, or in sport.
branches.cn: 事故这条线：多数 injury 在交通、工作或运动中突然发生。

branches.en: THE TEAM: a squad is chosen around who is free of injury.
branches.cn: 球队这条线：阵容往往取决于谁没有伤病。

branches.en: THE SPOT: the injury itself can be pointed at and treated.
branches.cn: 伤处这条线：injury 可以被指认，也可以被处理。

branches.en: THE COURT: law treats harm to a name as an injury too.
branches.cn: 法庭这条线：法律也把名誉受损视为 injury。

branches.en: THE THREAD: in every sense something that should be whole is broken.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：每个义项里，本应完整的某物都被破坏了。

intro.en: Injury keeps the Latin noun ending on the root for law and wrong.
intro.cn: injury 在「法、不义」词根上保留了拉丁语名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin ius, iniuria and iniurius are recorded, along with iustitia.

definition_zh: 墨水；油墨；（印刷、媒体）文字
definition_en: coloured liquid used for writing, printing, or drawing
core_image: 笔尖在纸上一按，留下一个深色的圆点
scene: 书桌上摊着一封写到一半的信。The ink had not dried, so the words smeared when he folded the sheet.
sceneCN: 这里 ink 是「墨水」（第 1 个义项：用于书写或印刷的有色液体）；句意为墨迹还没干，他折纸时字迹就抹花了。图中可辨识物件：墨水瓶、信封、钢笔。

pos.zh: 名词：墨水；油墨；文字宣传

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「墨黑的；沾了墨的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「墨黑；漆黑」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「沾上墨的」

senses.title: Liquid for writing
senses.definition: coloured liquid used with a pen for writing or drawing
senses.definitionCN: 配合笔用来书写或绘画的有色液体
senses.example: The letter was written in blue ink.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信是用蓝墨水写的。
senses.why: Greek enkauston named a burnt-in purple ink used by rulers, from en "in" and kaiein "to burn".
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 enkauston 指帝王用的「烧制」紫墨，由 en「在内」与 kaiein「烧」构成。

senses.title: Coloured paste for printing
senses.definition: thick coloured liquid used in printing machines
senses.definitionCN: 印刷机器所用的浓稠有色液体
senses.example: The printing ink dried faster than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷油墨干得比预想中快。
senses.why: Printing adapted the same substance to rollers and plates instead of nibs.
senses.whyCN: 印刷把这同一种物质从笔尖转用到滚筒与印版上。

senses.title: Words in print or the press
senses.definition: written publicity or coverage, especially in newspapers; often used in phrases with the press
senses.definitionCN: 尤指报纸上的文字报道或宣传，常见于与报界相关的短语中
senses.example: The scandal got plenty of ink in the local press.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩丑闻在当地报纸上占了不少篇幅。
senses.why: What is printed becomes ink as a habit of speech: coverage is measured by the litres of it consumed.
senses.whyCN: 被印出来的东西在口语里就成了 ink：报道量以耗掉多少「墨」来衡量。

intro.en: Ink reached English through Old French from a Greek word for a purple writing fluid.
intro.cn: ink 经由古法语进入英语，源自希腊语指紫色书写液体的词。

items.en: Enkauston meant "burnt in", from en "in" and kaiein "to burn", and named a purple ink.
items.cn: enkauston 意为「烧进去的」，由 en「在内」与 kaiein「烧」构成，指一种紫墨。

items.en: Latin took the word as encautum, a name for the purple ink used for imperial documents.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 encautum，指用于帝王文书的紫色墨水。

items.en: Old French enque shortened the word to a single syllable before it crossed the Channel.
items.cn: 古法语 enque 把词缩短为一个音节，随后它跨过海峡进入英语。

items.en: English ink is recorded from the thirteenth century, first for writing ink.
items.cn: 英语 ink 自十三世纪有记录，最初指书写用墨。

items.en: Printing and journalism broadened it from a fluid to the words it carries.
items.cn: 印刷与新闻业把它从一种液体扩展到它所承载的文字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that sound similar; the near-meaning group gathers writing and printing fluids.
note.cn: 形近组收读音相近的短词；近义组收书写与印刷用的液体。

entries.definition: To use the mind; it only rhymes with ink.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「想」，只是与 ink 押韵，词源不同。

entries.definition: A connection between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「连接」，词源不同。

entries.definition: Black as ink, or stained with it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「墨黑的、沾墨的」，由本词派生。

entries.definition: A substance used to colour cloth or hair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「染料」，用于给布料或头发上色。

entries.definition: Colouring matter, natural or in paint.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「颜料、色素」，天然或制画用。

entries.definition: The powder used in laser printers instead of ink.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「墨粉」，激光打印机中代替墨水使用。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek burning root and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用希腊语「烧」的词根，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Kaiein is to burn: the first fine ink was literally burned into the page.
normal.cn: kaiein 是「烧」：最早的精细墨汁真是「烧」进纸里的。

normal.en: ink, inky, inkiness: the noun first, the adjective after.
normal.cn: ink、inky、inkiness：先名词，再形容词与名词。

normal.en: Write in ink if you want the record to last.
normal.cn: 想让记录持久，就用 ink 书写。

normal.en: A pen runs out of ink at the worst time.
normal.cn: 钢笔总在最糟的时候没墨。

normal.en: To get ink in the press means to be written about.
normal.cn: get ink in the press 意为被媒体写进报道。

abstract.en: Picture one dark drop sinking into paper and spreading along the fibres.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴深色液体渗入纸中，沿着纤维散开。

abstract.en: Ink is a liquid that becomes a thought the moment it dries.
abstract.cn: 墨是一种液体，干透的那一刻就成了思想。

abstract.en: A signature in ink is a promise that cannot easily be taken back.
abstract.cn: 用墨写下的签名是不易收回的承诺。

examples.en: Please sign the form in black ink.
examples.cn: 请用黑色墨水在表格上签名。

examples.en: The ink on the old letters has faded to brown.
examples.cn: 旧信上的墨迹已褪成褐色。

examples.en: The story received little ink in the national press.

root: 希腊语 enkauston「烧进去的」由 en「在内」+ kaiein「烧」构成，指帝王用的紫墨；拉丁语作 encautum，古法语缩为 enque，十三世纪入英语作 ink。印刷与新闻业又把它引申为「文字、报道」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: writing ink, printing ink, and the words that ink puts on paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：书写墨水、印刷油墨，以及墨落在纸上的那些文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nib touches paper and leaves one dark drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔尖触纸，留下一个深色圆点。

branches.en: THE PEN: ink is what makes a pen leave a mark.
branches.cn: 钢笔这条线：ink 让笔留下痕迹。

branches.en: THE INKWELL: a small bottle on the desk kept the writing going.
branches.cn: 墨水瓶这条线：桌上的小瓶让书写得以继续。

branches.en: THE PRESS: printing machines use thicker ink on rollers.
branches.cn: 印刷这条线：印刷机在滚筒上使用更稠的油墨。

branches.en: THE PAPER: the news counts its coverage in ink.
branches.cn: 报纸这条线：新闻以「墨」的量计算报道篇幅。

branches.en: THE THREAD: ink is matter that turns into meaning when it dries.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：墨是干透后化为意义的物质。

intro.en: Ink is a much shortened Greek compound; English only adds simple endings to it.
intro.cn: ink 是高度简化的希腊语复合词，英语只给它加简单词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek enkauston was taken into Latin as encautum, the form that travelled into French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 enkauston 被拉丁语借作 encautum，这一形式再传入法语与英语。

items.example: It marks something put in by burning.
The Latin shortening of the Greek word.
items.exampleCN: 希腊词的拉丁缩略形式。

items.example: The French form that crossed to England.
items.exampleCN: 这是传入英国的法语形式。

definition_zh: 小旅店；客栈；（旧式）小酒馆
definition_en: a small hotel or pub, especially an old one in the country
core_image: 路边一栋木屋，门口的灯笼亮着，远处旅人正牵马走来
scene: 傍晚的山道上起了雾，马车夫急着找地方过夜。They stopped at a small inn where the fire was already burning.
sceneCN: 这里 inn 是「小旅店」（第 1 个义项：供旅人住宿的小旅馆）；句意为他们在一家小旅店停下，炉火已经烧了起来。图中可辨识物件：木屋、灯笼、马。

pos.zh: 名词：小旅店；客栈；小酒馆

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 keeper 构成，义为「旅店老板」
由本词加后缀构成，义为「（板球）回合；执政期」
由本词加 yard 构成，义为「客栈后院」

senses.title: A small hotel
senses.definition: a small, usually old, hotel that provides rooms, meals, and drink
senses.definitionCN: 通常较古老的小旅馆，提供房间、饭菜与酒水
senses.example: We spent the night at an inn by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边一家小旅店过了夜。
senses.why: Old English inn meant a house or lodging, and it kept the sense of a place you dwell in.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 inn 意为「房屋、住处」，一直保留「可供安身的地方」之意。

senses.title: A pub or tavern
senses.definition: a pub or tavern, especially one that serves food and drink to travellers and locals
senses.definitionCN: 尤指为旅人与本地人提供饮食的酒馆
senses.example: The whole village meets at the inn on Friday nights.
senses.exampleCN: 每周五晚上全村人都在那家酒馆聚会。
senses.why: A lodging house that also pours drinks became the social centre of English villages.
senses.whyCN: 兼卖酒的客店成了英格兰乡村的社交中心。

intro.en: Inn is a native English word, not a Latin borrowing; it simply meant a place inside.
intro.cn: inn 是英语本族词，不是拉丁借词，本义只是「里面的一处地方」。

items.en: The Germanic root inn- meant "in, inside"; Old English inn as a noun was a dwelling or lodging.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 inn- 意为「在内、里面」；古英语 inn 作名词指住所或住处。

items.en: Inn is recorded in Old English for a house or a room, especially one used for sheltering travellers.
items.cn: inn 在古英语中已有记录，指房屋或房间，尤指供旅人栖身之所。

items.en: By the Middle Ages an inn was a public house where travellers paid for bed and board.
items.cn: 到中世纪，inn 成了供旅人付费住宿与进餐的公共场所。

items.en: The coaching era fixed the word to roadside buildings for stagecoach passengers.
items.cn: 驿站马车时代把这个词固定在为乘客服务的路边建筑上。

items.en: Modern inns are usually small and old, and the word often appears in names rather than descriptions.
items.cn: 现代 inn 大多小而古老，这个词更常出现在店名而非描述中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that look or sound close; the near-meaning group gathers types of lodging and drinking places.
note.cn: 形近组收形音相近的短词；近义组收住宿与饮酒场所。

entries.definition: The preposition of being inside; same old root, different function.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在内」；同源但用法不同。

entries.definition: The person who runs an inn.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「旅店老板」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: A turn at batting, or a period in power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「击球回合、任期」，由本词派生。

entries.definition: A larger, modern place to stay, usually with many rooms.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「旅馆」，多指规模较大的现代住宿。

entries.definition: A place whose main business is serving drinks.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酒馆」，主业是卖酒。

entries.definition: A small house, or simple accommodation for guests.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小屋、客舍」，住宿较为简单。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the native English root of being inside and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用本族语「在里面」的词根，以及这个词的搭配。

normal.en: Inn and in share one root: it is the place you go in to for the night.
normal.cn: inn 与 in 同源：就是夜里能进去过夜的地方。

normal.en: An innkeeper keeps an inn, exactly as the compound says.
normal.cn: innkeeper 就是 keep an inn 的人，复合词说得明明白白。

normal.en: Stay at an inn, not in an inn: the verb prefers the article-free phrase.
normal.cn: 说 stay at an inn，而不是 in an inn。

normal.en: A country inn is small, old and by the road.
normal.cn: country inn 小而旧，往往临路而立。

normal.en: Villages used to gather at the inn on Friday nights.
normal.cn: 过去村里人周五夜里都聚在酒馆。

abstract.en: Picture a lit lantern by a door on a dark road: inside is a bed and a fire.
abstract.cn: 想象黑路上门边亮着一盏灯：里面有床和炉火。

abstract.en: An inn is shelter turned into a business, hospitality given a price.
abstract.cn: 旅店是把栖身之所变成生意，给好客标上了价钱。

abstract.en: The word is old enough to make travel feel familiar before it arrives.
abstract.cn: 这个词足够古老，能让旅人在抵达之前就感到熟悉。

examples.en: We found a warm inn at the end of the road.
examples.cn: 我们在路尽头找到一家暖和的旅店。

examples.en: The inn serves dinner until nine.
examples.cn: 这家旅店供晚餐到九点。

examples.en: He grew up in a village inn run by his parents.
examples.cn: 他在父母经营的小旅店里长大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因」——因天色晚，进 inn 里歇一宿

root: 古英语 inn 来自日耳曼语词根 inn-「在内」，本指房屋或住处，中世纪起专指旅人付费住宿的公共场所；与介词 in 同源。派生词有 innkeeper、innings。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: a lodging house for travellers, and the pub that grew inside it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：供旅人住宿的客店，以及在客店里生长出来的酒馆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lantern by a door on a dark road promises bed and fire.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑路上门边的一盏灯许下床铺与炉火。

branches.en: THE BED: an inn is first a place to sleep on the way.
branches.cn: 床铺这条线：inn 首先是途中的睡觉之处。

branches.en: THE ROAD: coaching inns served the passengers of stagecoaches.
branches.cn: 道路这条线：coaching inn 服务驿站马车的乘客。

branches.en: THE BAR: the inn also poured drinks for locals.
branches.cn: 吧台这条线：inn 也为本地人供应酒水。

branches.en: THE VILLAGE: the inn became the social centre of the settlement.
branches.cn: 村庄这条线：inn 成了村子的社交中心。

branches.en: THE THREAD: both senses sell shelter, one of the body and one of the evening.
branches.cn: 线索这条线：两个义项都在出售栖身之所，一个供身体，一个供夜晚。

intro.en: Inn is a native Germanic word; its English family is made with ordinary compounds and endings.
intro.cn: inn 是日耳曼语本族词，英语词族由普通复合与词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Inn has no Latin source; the related forms below are English and Germanic rather than Latin.
latinIntro.cn: inn 没有拉丁语来源，下列相关形式属英语与日耳曼语而非拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: 它提供本词的基本意象。

items.exampleCN: 一个自有词义的扩展形式。
